pages.title: Test the rule a shortcut would try to bypass

blocks.code:
# Validação dos limites de autoridade e validade.
def test_restore_requires_two_distinct_reviewers(self):
    verified = self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "reviewer-a", 101)
    self.assertEqual(verified["state"], "verified")
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "reviewer-a", 102)
    result = self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "reviewer-b", 102)
    self.assertEqual((result["state"], result["epoch"]), ("restored", 1))

def test_owner_cannot_verify(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "customer", 101)
    self.assertEqual(self.store.read("case")["revision"], 0)

def test_expired_case_cannot_restore(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "expired"):
        self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 400)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The tests challenge three shortcuts: the same reviewer approving and restoring access, the requester verifying their own identity, and a decision being applied after its deadline. Each rejection must preserve the previous state. The test does not ask whether a screen displayed a message; it verifies that the prohibited mutation did not happen.

These restrictions are governance fixtures for the simulation. A real team could adopt another approval policy, provided the rule was explicit and tested. The important question in a Staff-level review is who has authority over each transition and how that authority remains valid under repetition and delay.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Resuming a case must not repeat restoration

blocks.code:
def test_stale_revision_cannot_repeat_verification(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "stale_revision"):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "b", 102)

def test_reopen_preserves_case_and_epoch(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    reopened = Recovery(self.path)
    self.assertEqual(reopened.read("case")["revision"], 1)
    reopened.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 102)
    self.assertEqual(Recovery(self.path).read("case")["epoch"], 1)

def test_cannot_skip_review_or_restore_twice(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "restore", "b", 101)
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 102)
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 2, "restore", "c", 103)
    self.assertEqual(self.store.read("case")["epoch"], 1)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: Reopening the Recovery object uses the same persisted file, demonstrating that the version and generation do not depend on the previous instance’s memory. The other tests reject a stale revision, an attempt to skip verification, and a second restoration.

All seven tests in the file passed, including checks for an invalid clock and revision type. They cover the local machine and its preconditions, but do not exercise concurrency with authenticated operators, real queues, or identity services. Nor do they measure biometric quality. The next implementation experiment would inject duplicate delivery and revocation between approval and application while retaining the same criterion: no access change without a valid decision.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Measure the queue without exposing its members

blocks.text: The central metric would be time to completed legitimate recovery, broken down by stage and technical reason for routing. An average alone would hide people stuck for days while simple cases finish quickly. I would track the tail of waiting times, the age of the oldest case, and repeat-contact rate, as well as the proportion of requests returning to the same stage without useful new information.

A second dimension measures protection: restorations later disputed, rejected attempts to use expired decisions, and blocked commands from old generations. These numbers must not reward a team for denying everything, nor should speed encourage approval without sufficient evidence. The dashboard must show both sides of the decision and support qualitative sample reviews with controlled access to details.

I would avoid identifying people, specific devices, or reviewers in aggregate metric labels. Individual investigations would remain in audit trails with a defined purpose and permissions. For accessibility, useful segmentation would follow the observed barrier, such as an unavailable camera or reading difficulty, without turning collection into intrusive classification. The intended result is to locate the operational and technical bottleneck with enough information to act while retaining the minimum necessary information about each account holder.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Launch exception paths with support prepared

blocks.text: The first delivery would not be a new identity algorithm. It would detect the technical failure earlier and prevent a futile sequence of capture attempts. A message could explain that the component is unavailable and route the person to the existing assisted path. This behavior should be validated with people using broken cameras, denied permissions, and limited-capability devices, including use with assistive technology.

Next, I would introduce case tracking to a controlled cohort. Support would need access to the same state the customer sees, differing only in the permitted level of detail. A migration that creates more states without preparing operators can increase transfers between teams. Each new state would therefore have an operational action, an owner, and an understandable exit criterion.

Automated restoration or identity integration would follow only after authorization, expiration, and revocation had been validated in a test environment. Rollback would keep open cases queryable and prevent reapplication of already confirmed decisions. I would define an operational intake limit so that the new journey did not collect requests faster than the team could review them. The experience must be sustainable for both the customer and the person resolving the exception.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Accessibility is part of the security surface

blocks.text: Ambiguous instructions can make people repeat movements, seek unsuitable environments, or share information through the wrong channels. I would treat journey clarity as a security control: explain what will be requested, where information is sent, and what happens next. That does not mean revealing fraud rules. It means reducing the gap between a legitimate action and an improvised workaround that exposes the customer.

In the proposed Flutter interface, states would need accessible semantics, stable focus order, and announcements that do not rely exclusively on color or animation. A camera failure must not disappear so quickly that a screen reader cannot announce it. Validation would include enlarged text and app interruption, because recovery often takes place under less comfortable conditions than an ideal onboarding flow.

For performance, I would reduce repeated collection and loading steps that do not change the decision. The client could query status at a moderate frequency while relevant updates were propagated recoverably. The priority is not approval at any cost, but removing waits that add no verification. If a stage takes time because it depends on a person, the app should acknowledge that and provide accurate tracking rather than an endless spinner that looks like a technical failure.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: ADR: an explicit recovery process with limited authorization

blocks.text: The proposed decision is to represent recovery as a domain process separate from everyday login. One alternative would embed every exception in the same capture flow. That would simplify initial navigation, but make it difficult to understand attempts that span support, device replacement, and review. Another alternative would resolve everything manually through messages, providing considerable flexibility but little consistency in state, authorization, or tracking.

I would choose an explicit process because it makes the validity of each decision clear and limits what each step authorizes. Verifying a document need not mean enabling every financial operation. Restored access may require further risk checks under the applicable policy without turning the state machine into a universal shortcut. Those policies would be product and security decisions, not deductions from the public report.

The accepted cost is maintaining contracts between identity, review, and support. The design must also avoid bureaucracy: states should exist only when they change responsibility, authorization, or useful information. I would revisit the ADR if most exceptions could be resolved through reliable local diagnosis, if manual operations became the dominant bottleneck, or if new device capabilities reduced the need for collection. The choice would be reviewed against evidence of legitimate resolution and protection, not the number of steps.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: EM execution: the capacity to resolve cases, not merely receive them

blocks.text: As an EM, I would begin with a workshop on real cases already authorized for analysis, bringing together support, identity, risk, mobile, and accessibility. The output would be a matrix of barriers, owners, and existing paths. The broken-camera report would inform one category without being used to claim prevalence. I would separate improvements to clarity, process changes, and authorization changes because they have different risks and dependencies.

The plan would have small deliverables: understandable diagnosis, routing with context, shared state, and transactional integration with identity. Each would require a demonstration under failure, an operational review, and the capacity to track outcomes. As a Staff engineer, I would focus on decision validity across boundaries, session generation, and persistent transitions. The lab is an artifact for technical discussion, not a substitute for security review.

Value could be calculated through support minutes avoided, fewer repeat contacts, and shorter periods without access for legitimate account holders. Any retention gain would require an appropriate comparison, and fraud costs or additional review costs would be deducted. The leadership question would be: “Are we removing a barrier that adds no security, or simply shifting work to another team?” The answer must be visible in case resolution and protection metrics, not just screen conversion.

chapters.title: A notification should help someone decide
chapters.subtitle: Communication contracts, late privacy enforcement, and usefulness
chapters.source_title: NuCommunity — Nubank app push notifications omit the amount (suggestions)

pages.title: Enough information, deliberate disclosure

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.
Screenshot published by a customer on NuCommunity, kept in Portuguese. Context and limitations are available in the source.

blocks.text: The public suggestion collects examples of investment income, cashback, and bill notifications that, according to the author, omitted amounts. The attached images provide context for the complaint, but do not reveal all privacy preferences or the version currently available. The opportunity is not to conclude that every notification should display money. It is to build a content policy that helps people decide while respecting the disclosure context they have chosen.

I would begin by asking what task the message enables someone to complete. An alert may confirm that something happened, request an action, or highlight a deadline. Each purpose needs different fields. An amount may prevent an unnecessary app opening; on a locked screen visible to other people, the same amount may disclose information the account holder would prefer to keep private. The experience must make this choice understandable rather than accidental.

This chapter’s proposal combines an event contract, a message catalog, versioned preferences, and late enforcement of the privacy policy. The lab queues synthetic facts, changes the preference before sending, and verifies the final content. It does not connect to push providers. Its purpose is to show that the moment at which a policy is evaluated is part of system correctness, just as much as the sentence displayed on screen.

sources.title: NuCommunity — Nubank app push notifications omit the amount (suggestions)

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: A financial fact is not notification copy

blocks.text: A domain event should describe what happened without embedding a ready-made sentence for a particular language or device. The communication catalog interprets that fact, decides whether there is a relevant message, and applies the presentation policy. Separating these responsibilities allows copy to be corrected without changing event semantics and privacy to evolve without requiring every financial producer to understand each mobile platform’s particularities.

The proposed contract contains event_id, schema version, event type, account holder, and only the necessary data. Preferences have a different lifecycle: they can change while a message waits in the queue. Storing final copy with an exposed amount when the event is produced would therefore be insufficient. The proposal reads the current policy close to delivery and includes its version in the operational evidence.

There are at least four communication states: eligible, suppressed, accepted by the provider, and displayed or opened when that information is available. Acceptance does not prove reading, and the absence of an open event does not prove failure. The lab models only local acceptance and suppression. Product decisions must avoid treating “sent” as certainty that the customer learned about a financial fact or had an effective opportunity to act.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Render close to delivery and record the decision

blocks.title: Render close to delivery and record the decision
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: The renderer is the boundary where a financial fact becomes text potentially visible outside the app. It needs the current preference and catalog version. If the preference query is unavailable, the proposed policy falls back to content without an amount or suppresses the message, depending on its purpose. Consent is not assumed because the preferences service is down.

The queue preserves event identity and version; duplicates must not generate repeated messages indefinitely. The audit record captures the communication decision and its policy parameters, avoiding storage of the sensitive body when a controlled reference is enough. The external provider remains an important boundary: after it accepts a payload, withdrawing it may no longer be possible.

Kafka would be an asynchronous transport option, but would not replace deduplication of the effect at the provider boundary. The lab keeps its queue and deduplication in memory to isolate content rules, without claiming durability or actual delivery.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Apply privacy at the last controllable point

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The method first recognizes a delivery already accepted in the model and avoids repeating it. For a pending message, it reads the current preference. The default hides the amount; disclosure requires explicit enablement. Monetary formatting uses divmod on integer cents, without binary floating-point rounding.

The “accepted” result is only the simulated provider’s response. After that point, changing the preference cannot recall a message already delivered, and the lab makes no such promise. A real implementation would also need to bound the interval between reading the preference and sending, handle an unavailable read, and document the revocation boundary.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Clojure: a message catalog as data

blocks.code:
(def templates
  {:income {:title "Atualização financeira"
            :private-body "Consulte os detalhes no aplicativo."}
   :cashback {:title "Cashback disponível"
              :private-body "Veja a atualização no aplicativo."}})

(defn cents-label [cents]
  (str "R$ " (quot cents 100) ","
       (format "%02d" (mod cents 100))))

(defn render-message [event preference]
  ;; Catálogo e contrato propostos; sem envio neste exemplo.
  (when-not (= 1 (:schema-version event))
    (throw (ex-info "unsupported-schema" {})))
  (when-not (true? (:enabled? preference))
    (throw (ex-info "communication-suppressed" {})))
  (let [template (get templates (:kind event))
        amount (:amount-cents event)]
    (when-not (and template (integer? amount) (<= 0 amount))
      (throw (ex-info "invalid-event" {})))
    {:title (:title template)
     :body (if (true? (:show-values? preference))
             (str "Crédito disponível: " (cents-label amount))
             (:private-body template))
     :policy-version (:version preference)}))
blocks.caption: Proposed catalog and function; Clojure not executed.

blocks.text: The example makes the catalog inspectable and keeps the privacy decision in a function separate from transport. This facilitates tests of wording, amounts, and preference combinations. The field names and sentences are proposals in this book, not actual Nubank contracts.

A production catalog would need governance for translation, accessibility, and purpose, alongside disclosure review. The function does not resolve the race between revocation and sending, nor does it replace authorization to query account-holder information. It must not receive unvalidated monetary values from arbitrary sources either. This Clojure excerpt is educational and was neither compiled nor executed.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Version content without breaking older consumers

blocks.text: The event schema and message version solve different problems. The former defines fields and meaning; the latter identifies how those fields were presented. A title change may be compatible with the same event, whereas introducing a new financial state may require a consumer update. I would record these versions separately so that investigations do not have to reconstruct communication from the code running in production today.

In transport, event_id must remain stable when a producer repeats publication. Deduplication must detect the same identifier reappearing with different content, since that signals a contract error. The lab rejects this reuse. For a real persistent queue, I would define retention, partitioning, and handling of unrecognized events, ensuring that a producer update could not silently suppress critical messages without alerting the owner.

Preferences also need versions to explain which policy was applied. That does not authorize storing a complete history of personal information inside the event. A minimal operational record can reference a policy and a decision, with restricted access to details when necessary. In the customer’s settings, the configuration must have a stable meaning: “hide amounts in notifications” must not accidentally hide only some categories. Any exceptions should be explicit and justified.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Reject ambiguity before generating copy

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: Input validation checks the set of fields, integer version, category, and monetary type. Reusing event_id with different content creates a conflict. Preferences require actual booleans: the string false cannot be interpreted as permission to expose amounts. A valid configuration increments the preference version, making it possible to recognize that a communication decision occurred under a different policy.

The model is deliberately strict: a producer adding fields must negotiate the contract instead of relying on silent acceptance. That choice suits the lab; a real platform could adopt extensible compatibility with well-defined rules. The in-memory queue does not survive a restart, so the tests on this page verify semantics, not transport reliability.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: A preference changes between production and delivery

blocks.code:
def test_privacy_changed_while_queued_is_respected(self):
    self.n.configure("u", show_values=True)
    self.n.enqueue(self.event)
    self.n.configure("u", show_values=False)
    self.assertNotIn("123", str(self.n.deliver("e1")))

def test_opt_out_suppresses_delivery(self):
    self.n.enqueue(self.event)
    self.n.configure("u", enabled=False)
    self.assertEqual(self.n.deliver("e1"), {"status": "suppressed"})
    self.assertEqual(len(self.n.sent), 0)

def test_replay_is_identical(self):
    self.n.enqueue(self.event)
    first = self.n.deliver("e1")
    self.n.enqueue(self.event)
    self.assertEqual(self.n.deliver("e1"), first)
    self.assertEqual(len(self.n.sent), 1)

def test_payload_conflict_is_rejected(self):
    self.n.enqueue(self.event)
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.n.enqueue(dict(self.event, amount_cents=999))
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The privacy test changes the preference after the event is queued. That ordering reproduces a window an isolated screen test would miss. Another scenario disables communication and verifies that the message does not enter the set of accepted deliveries. Retry and conflict tests complete the protection without depending on an external provider.

The file passed eight tests, including rejection of preferences and versions with incorrect types. The evidence does not cover lock-screen presentation, screen readers, or operating-system behavior. Those layers would need device tests and research. The lab demonstrates only that the local renderer respects the preference it reads before its simulated delivery.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Measure usefulness without optimizing for curiosity

blocks.text: Open rate is an ambiguous signal for financial notifications. A clear message may reduce opens because it already answered the question; an incomplete message may increase them because it forces the customer to investigate. I would not use opens as a standalone objective. Evaluation would begin with comprehension: can the person identify what happened, know whether they need to act, and recognize where to find details without misinterpreting the situation?

The proposed operational metrics would separate eligible events, messages suppressed by preference, provider acceptance, and rendering failures. Increased suppression may be the correct behavior after a preference change, not a regression. Alerts would look for unexpected deviations by category and version using a low-cardinality vocabulary. Financial amounts, recipients, and full message bodies would not become metric labels.

In a product experiment, I would measure queries motivated solely by missing information, contacts associated with the message, and adherence to preferences. Participants could explain the message without executing an operation, reducing test risk. The experience must also be evaluated on locked screens, with enlarged fonts, and with screen readers. Success would mean sufficient information and deliberate disclosure, not maximizing message volume or time spent in the app.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Migrate a catalog without overwhelming the customer

blocks.text: Rollout would begin with an inventory of notification types, their producers, available fields, and purposes. Before changing copy, I would identify transactional messages, reminders, and optional communications. This classification informs preferences, fallback, and urgency. The public post is a starting point for a few categories, not a justification for indiscriminate changes to every app message.

I would validate the new renderer in comparison mode: generate the candidate version without sending it, then check field and policy differences using synthetic data or properly authorized, minimized data. A small cohort would then receive a single revised category. Per-recipient and per-event limits would prevent an integration failure from causing mass repetition. Support would have examples of old and new messages to recognize questions arising during the transition.

Rollback must preserve event_id and delivery records. Reprocessing the backlog with the previous catalog must not resend everything already accepted. Privacy changes must not be silently reversed when the binary is rolled back either. I would treat preferences as a persistent customer contract independent of renderer version. Expansion would depend on evidence of comprehension and the absence of unexpected disclosure, not technical stability alone.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: The message body crosses a new boundary

blocks.text: Once text leaves the app, it may appear on a locked screen, a watch, system history, and provider infrastructure. Minimization must therefore happen before sending, not merely through a visual layer inside the app. Hiding an amount on an internal screen does not remove it from a payload already transmitted. The proposal would keep sensitive content out of the body when the preference does not authorize its disclosure.

Action links also need careful design. An embedded identifier cannot act as a credential for reading a transaction. When opening the message, the app must authenticate the required context and resolve the destination with authorization. I would avoid personal information in URLs and check link behavior after logout, device replacement, or session recovery. An expired destination should provide guidance without exposing old data.

On cost, reading preferences for every delivery may add latency and load. Choosing between a direct read and a cache requires an explicit staleness limit and a conservative policy when that limit cannot be guaranteed. Optimizing this path without modeling revocation could make the system fast and incorrect. Performance would be evaluated alongside preference propagation time, keeping both objectives visible.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: ADR: centralized rendering with distributed responsibility

blocks.text: The proposed decision centralizes cross-cutting content and privacy rules while keeping ownership of event meaning in the producing domain. Allowing every team to write its own push messages makes local delivery easier but tends to create variations in wording, fields, and policy. Making a central service decide every financial fact as well would concentrate too much responsibility and weaken domain clarity.

I would choose a governed catalog and per-event contracts. The producing team would guarantee semantics and identity; the communication platform would guarantee rendering, policy, and provider integration; product and design would guarantee comprehension and accessibility. This division would have contract tests on both sides. An unknown message should not automatically become generic copy if doing so concealed an important customer action.

The accepted cost is additional coordination when introducing new event types. The intended benefit is consistent privacy and content changes without reimplementing the rule in every domain. I would revisit the ADR if the catalog became a delivery bottleneck or categories with different guarantees required operational isolation. The solution is not one template for everything: it is a common mechanism for applying explicit choices, with clear ownership of every message and its purpose.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: EM and Staff: govern communication as a product

blocks.text: As an EM, I would form a small group spanning communications, mobile, the financial domain, and privacy to review the categories with the greatest friction. The initial delivery would be a catalog with an owner, purpose, required fields, and defined behavior when data is missing. Every change would include authorized real or synthetic examples and a comprehension test. This prevents the project from becoming a sequence of copy edits that never addresses the source of inconsistencies.

As a Staff engineer, I would review event identity, the preference enforcement boundary, and the distinction between provider acceptance and the perceived effect. I would also require a reprocessing strategy that preserves deduplication. Technical contribution becomes especially valuable when several teams publish events and one contract failure can affect communications with different purposes. The lab provides a small foundation for discussing these invariants without claiming knowledge of internal infrastructure.

Value would be expressed through time saved on queries, fewer contacts, and comprehension, including operational and review costs. An increase in opens would not be presented as a benefit if incomplete messages caused it. My interview question would be: “How do we prove that the preference applied to a message was the correct one at the last moment when we could still control its disclosure?” The answer connects product, engineering, and operational responsibility.

chapters.title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete
chapters.subtitle: Provenance, consent, and completeness contracts
chapters.source_title: NuCommunity — Open Finance: Mercado Pago Cofrinhos do not appear in Nubank

pages.title: A subtotal must acknowledge what it does not know

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.

blocks.text: The report dated October 3, 2026 distinguishes two observations: balances and transactions from another institution appeared in Nubank, but Cofrinhos positions did not appear in the investment aggregator. The participant does not claim certainty about the cause. The post therefore cannot establish a Nubank defect or an obligation to provide that resource. The evidence supports investigating coverage, consent, availability, and data interpretation.

Financial aggregation has two products: the values displayed and an explanation of how complete that view is. Adding only what arrived may be mathematically correct yet semantically misleading if the result appears to represent all assets. My proposal would maintain state by institution and resource, including provenance, freshness, and the reason for absence. Not receiving a position must not automatically be interpreted as a zero-value position.

This chapter’s lab models that distinction with complete, unsupported, and unavailable states, alongside missing or stale resources. When there are gaps, the sum is explicitly a known subtotal. There is no connection to real banking APIs. The demonstration makes an important product decision verifiable: partial information can remain useful, provided the app does not convey more certainty than the available evidence supports.

sources.title: NuCommunity — Open Finance: Mercado Pago Cofrinhos do not appear in Nubank

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Completeness is a property of the requested set

blocks.text: A complete resource does not make a complete portfolio. The answer depends on the resources expected for that connection and the scope authorized by the customer. If the current account was synchronized but investments were not queried, the system must preserve that distinction. I would represent a coverage matrix combining participant, product type, consent, and integration capability, avoiding a single “connected” indicator that conceals different situations.

Zero means a valid source reported no value for that resource. Unsupported means the resource is outside the capability being considered. Unavailable means the capability exists, but the query did not return a usable answer at that moment. Missing means there is not yet sufficient observation. These states may lead to different actions: explaining coverage, waiting, retrying a query, or reviewing consent without forcing the customer to disconnect everything.

Freshness must also be defined. A position valid yesterday may be useful as history and unsuitable for a total presented as current. The proposal stores observed_at and an orderable version per resource, with an age limit determined by purpose. The lab excludes values outside that limit from the subtotal and records the gap. A real experience could show the last known value separately, provided its age and meaning were unambiguous.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Provenance by resource, not a generic connection badge

blocks.title: Provenance by resource, not a generic connection badge
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: Normalization happens per resource to preserve differences between external responses. The adapter does not decide that absence means zero; it supplies data and context for validation. The projection retains the result together with its source, version, and observation time. The aggregator combines only values that satisfy the freshness policy and returns gaps as part of the contract, not as a detail hidden in logs.

Consent spans the entire flow. A response already in transit before revocation must be recognized as belonging to the old generation and must not silently repopulate the view. The lab uses consent_epoch to demonstrate that barrier, but does not implement actual consent protocols.

The design makes it possible to investigate where information disappeared: capability, authorization, response, transformation, or presentation. This separation helps teams work with partners without assigning blame prematurely. The interface receives enough information to explain the boundary and offer an action proportionate to the observed gap.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Add known values without hiding gaps

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The function walks the expected set and assigns a reason to each resource that cannot contribute. A valid zero participates normally in the sum; a missing position is not replaced with zero. The complete field depends on there being no gaps, and revocation returns an unavailable value rather than an apparently empty total.

A zero subtotal with complete=false needs explicit presentation: “known subtotal,” accompanied by the gaps. The lab does not implement the interface. It also uses a uniform age limit to simplify testing; in a real product, the freshness policy would be defined by resource type and purpose.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Clojure: partial results as first-class data

blocks.code:
(defn usable? [now max-age resource]
  (and (= :complete (:status resource))
       (integer? (:cents resource))
       (<= 0 (- now (:observed-at resource)) max-age)))

(defn aggregate [expected resources now max-age]
  ;; Contrato proposto: total conhecido sempre vem com cobertura.
  (reduce
    (fn [acc key]
      (let [resource (get resources key)]
        (if (usable? now max-age resource)
          (update acc :known-cents + (:cents resource))
          (assoc-in acc [:gaps key]
            (cond
              (nil? resource) :missing
              (not= :complete (:status resource))
              (:status resource)
              :else :stale-or-future)))))
    {:known-cents 0 :gaps {}}
    expected))

(defn presentation [result]
  (assoc result :label
    (if (empty? (:gaps result))
      :covered-total :known-subtotal)))
blocks.caption: Proposed teaching contract and functions; Clojure not executed.

blocks.text: The proposed structure carries gaps alongside the subtotal. This reduces the likelihood of an intermediate layer discarding the context and presenting only a number. The presentation function selects a label without changing the sum, making it clear that completeness is a semantic decision distinct from arithmetic.

The excerpt assumes previously validated resources and does not implement consent, persistence, or event ordering. It was not executed in Clojure. Its role in this chapter is to explore the contract between aggregation and presentation. A real implementation would need to test older consumers to ensure they do not ignore gaps and display known-cents as complete assets.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: A coverage contract requires a shared vocabulary

blocks.text: The proposed response would contain known_cents, coverage_complete, gaps, and freshness references for each resource. Currency would also be mandatory: adding different currencies without an explicit conversion would produce a meaningless number. The lab assumes a single unit in cents and does not handle foreign exchange. This restriction is stated in scope to prevent the example’s simplicity from being mistaken for a complete asset aggregator.

Each gap would need a stable reason that the app can present and support can investigate. A participant’s technical codes should not flow directly into customer-facing copy. The adapter would map them into domain categories while retaining diagnostic details in a controlled channel. When the cause is uncertain, the category must acknowledge that uncertainty instead of automatically blaming the user or the external institution.

Contract evolution also includes new resources. The expected set must be versioned or derived from a known capability, because adding a category may turn a previously complete view into a partial one. That may be correct, but it needs explanation. I would treat the coverage matrix as an operational product with an owner, tests, and review, not an informal exception list maintained only by support.

pages.title: Reject old events and preserve meaning

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The method applies the consent barrier before considering the content. It then validates the resource and requires unknown states to carry cents=None. Per-resource versions prevent a delayed response from replacing a newer observation. The boolean result indicates whether the projection changed.

The lab ignores equal or older versions. A real implementation should investigate the same version arriving with different content, for example through a fingerprint comparison, rather than treating the anomaly as a normal duplicate. The sequence must also come from a trusted contract or be assigned at the correct ingestion point; arrival time alone does not necessarily establish business order.

pages.title: Four tests against false precision

blocks.code:
def test_partial_is_not_complete(self):
    self.p.apply("account", self.resource())
    self.assertEqual(self.p.summarize(110),
                     dict(cents=100, complete=False,
                          gaps={"investment": "missing"}))

def test_zero_is_a_real_complete_position(self):
    self.p.apply("account", self.resource())
    self.p.apply("investment", self.resource(0))
    self.assertTrue(self.p.summarize(110)["complete"])

def test_unsupported_requires_none(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.p.apply("investment", self.resource(0, status="unsupported"))
    self.p.apply("investment", self.resource(None, status="unsupported"))
    self.assertEqual(self.p.summarize(110)["gaps"]["investment"], "unsupported")

def test_old_or_duplicate_events_do_not_overwrite(self):
    self.p.apply("account", self.resource(200, sequence=2))
    self.assertFalse(self.p.apply("account", self.resource(100)))
    self.assertFalse(self.p.apply("account", self.resource(300, sequence=2)))
    self.assertEqual(self.p.summarize(110)["cents"], 200)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The scenarios separate four situations that may look similar: only some resources have arrived, a resource reported zero, a resource is unsupported, and an old version arrived after a newer one. The sum alone cannot distinguish them, so the tests also check coverage and the reason for each gap.

The complete file passed eight tests, covering an invalid sequence, expired observation, future timestamp, and revocation with an event in transit. No real Open Finance query was made. The evidence demonstrates the local contract and provides fixtures for a future integration, which would need to validate scopes, schemas, and the behavior of authorized participants.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Observability that locates the incomplete boundary

blocks.text: The proposed dashboard would start with the proportion of connections with complete coverage and the distribution of gap reasons. It would then show observation age, validation failures, and responses discarded because of consent generation. A technically active connection with only some resources synchronized should not be counted in the same way as a complete, current view. The metric must reflect the contract delivered to the customer.

I would segment by participant and resource class where cardinality is controlled, avoiding identification of individual accounts. A decline concentrated in one resource may indicate a contract change; widespread failures may point to shared infrastructure or an internal policy. These signals guide investigation but do not establish a cause without evidence. The runbook would check authorization, availability, received response, transformation, and presentation in that order.

I would also measure repeated reconnections, because asking users to renew consent may be the wrong solution for an unsupported resource. The objective is to reduce futile actions and diagnosis time. Alerts must distinguish expected data absence from a coverage regression. A new product that is not yet supported should not trigger the same incident as the interruption of a previously working integration.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Launch transparency before promising broader coverage

blocks.text: The first delivery could improve the subtotal label and show the last update without adding new participants or products. That would require confirming that provenance data already exists or instrumenting its collection safely. Displaying an arbitrary date merely to fill the screen would create another false certainty. The displayed information must correspond to observation, processing, or query time, with a defined meaning.

Next, I would validate the coverage matrix with authorized test accounts and known scenarios. Each participant-resource combination would have cases for a positive value, zero, missing permission, unavailability, and a delayed response. Gradual rollout would allow comparison of old and new classifications, checking that consumers preserve the meaning of partial. A change in the apparent total would need careful explanation so it did not look like money had disappeared.

Rollback must not restore an incomplete number as though it were complete. A presentation flag can change how the explanation is shown, but must not erase coverage semantics. I would preserve that invariant in the contract. Support for new resources would expand through a separate project with its own integration dependencies and acceptance criteria, keeping transparency distinct from promises of capability not yet demonstrated.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Revoked consent and a delayed response

blocks.text: An integration may be querying data when the customer revokes consent. If the system checks state only when the request begins, a delayed response can repopulate a projection that was just cleared. The proposed generation handles the logical part of that problem: the response carries the context under which it was requested, and the update handler checks that the context is still valid before publishing the change.

The lab clears resources on revocation and rejects events from an old generation. A real implementation would need to define handling of copies, caches, history, and applicable retention obligations with privacy and security owners. The example does not establish legal rules. It makes a technical condition explicit: the decision to display data must respect the authorization valid at the point of use, not only at the start of asynchronous work.

For performance, I would avoid querying every institution on each app opening. Projections can provide fast reads if they carry provenance and freshness limits. The cost is handling partial states and delays. The benefit does not justify hiding those states. The architecture question would be which resources tolerate which age for each purpose, preserving a useful experience without presenting an old observation as the current state.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: ADR: explicit completeness instead of filling gaps with zero

blocks.text: The proposed decision keeps absence and zero semantically distinct. Filling everything with zero simplifies the sum and the interface but destroys coverage information. Hiding the whole aggregator whenever one resource is missing avoids false precision, yet removes the usefulness of valid data and may make the experience unstable. I would choose a known subtotal accompanied by gaps and freshness information, with tested presentation.

This decision requires consumers to treat partial state as a normal condition. Adding an optional field and hoping every screen uses it correctly is not enough. Contracts and integration tests must demonstrate that a partial value does not appear under a complete-total label. It is also necessary to define when the experience stops being useful, for example when no relevant resource is current, so it can show unavailability rather than an empty subtotal without context.

The accepted cost is greater complexity in the domain and its communication. The intended return is trust and faster diagnosis. I would revisit the ADR if a stronger coverage guarantee became available or research showed that the chosen vocabulary confused customers. I would change presentation and contract together while preserving the fundamental distinction between what was observed, what was not observed, and what is outside scope.

pages.chapter_title: Open Finance must show what is still incomplete

pages.title: Leadership across institutions, product, and support

blocks.text: As an EM, I would structure the work into two tracks: quality of explanation and broader coverage. The first can progress through state and provenance; the second depends on participant contracts and capabilities. Combining them creates promises the team does not control. An integration owner would maintain the resource matrix while product and support validated whether gap reasons can guide people without unnecessary reconnections.

As a Staff engineer, I would review the consent boundary, update ordering, and subtotal semantics. Investigation would begin with the evidence received, not an assumed defect at the partner or Nubank. This approach improves technical discussion and makes it easier to demonstrate which layer needs to change. The lab provides small examples every team can reproduce without access to real financial data.

Value would be estimated through fewer support requests, avoided reconnections, and diagnosis time. Retention or incremental activation would enter the assessment only after an appropriate experiment. My interview question would be: “When we display an aggregate number, what completeness contract does that number carry, and how does the customer understand its boundaries?” A good answer combines data modeling, experience, integration, and operational responsibility.

chapters.subtitle: Civil-date scheduling, preferences, and job revalidation
chapters.source_title: NuCommunity — Nubank’s payment assistant needs improvements

pages.title: Organize the next payment decision

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.
Screenshot published by a customer on NuCommunity, kept in Portuguese. Context and limitations are available in the source.

blocks.text: The NuCommunity post raises concerns about reminder timing, identifying the next due date, and navigating between months. It describes one participant’s experience and includes attached screenshots; it does not establish the product’s current state or demonstrate that a notification caused a late payment. The product question is more specific: does the assistant help someone recognize their next obligation without reconstructing a mental schedule from several screens?

I would treat viewing due dates and executing payments as different journeys. The first can reduce effort through ordering, wording, and state updates. The second involves authorization, funds, confirmation, and financial consequences. Adding a better list does not authorize payment automation, and increasing reminder volume does not guarantee organization. The project must preserve that boundary to improve the experience without introducing unexpected actions.

The proposal organizes obligations by civil date, makes the next due date explicit, and applies time preferences to reminders. The lab tests month changes, payment before sending, duplicates, and time-zone rules, including ambiguous or nonexistent times in another country. These scenarios do not describe confirmed Nubank problems; they are engineering conditions a scheduling solution must resolve predictably before expansion.

sources.title: NuCommunity — Nubank’s payment assistant needs improvements

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: A due date is a civil date; sending happens at an instant

blocks.text: A bill due on the first of November has a business date. A reminder sent at nine in the morning has an instant that depends on the selected time zone. Storing both as though they were the same timestamp creates ambiguity: converting midnight UTC into another zone can shift the date the customer understands as the due date. I would keep due_date as a civil date and reminder_at as an instant calculated from an explicit preference and zone.

An obligation also has an identity and version. If its amount, due date, or state changes, a previously generated job may become stale. The dispatcher must compare the current version before sending. A paid state must not depend solely on an interface click; it needs to indicate the source and certainty of the available confirmation. When a bill is paid elsewhere and that has not yet been observed, the message should avoid asserting a debt as a definitive fact.

The lab uses increasing versions and invalidates a reminder when the obligation has been updated or paid. It does not integrate DDA, a banking calendar, holidays, or settlement. This reduction makes temporal discipline testable without mixing in external rules. The proposed interface could show the “next known due date” and allow details to be checked, keeping the information source and the remaining action clear.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: A schedule with explicit clocks and versions

blocks.title: A schedule with explicit clocks and versions
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: The planner turns a business date and a preference into a sending instant. The queue retains the obligation version used in that calculation. When the job becomes due, the dispatcher checks the current state: a paid, changed, or canceled bill makes the old work obsolete. The chronological query path does not depend on executing a payment or sending a message.

This proposed architecture accepts that a queue may deliver late or more than once. Reminder identity prevents local duplication, while a validity window prevents a message from arriving the following day after losing its context. Delay policy should vary by purpose; the lab chooses to expire a reminder when the civil date changes.

The test clock is passed as a parameter, allowing date boundaries to be reproduced without waiting for real time. Production operations would need to consider persistence, clock synchronization, preference changes, and notification-provider behavior.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Resolve times that do not exist on the local clock

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The function constructs candidates for the preferred time and checks the round trip between the local zone and UTC. A nonexistent time during a zone transition does not return to the same civil value, so the search advances to the first valid minute. When two occurrences exist, the synthetic policy chooses the earlier UTC instant.

This policy should be an explicit product decision, not an accidental library behavior. The code uses the standard library’s zoneinfo and the system’s available time-zone database. Tests include Berlin only to exercise transitions; this does not suggest that the Brazilian report involved daylight saving time.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Dart: a list ordered by due date need not execute anything

blocks.caption: Proposed presentation model; Dart/Flutter not executed.

blocks.text: The presentation model uses a civil date, preserves money in cents, and orders items with a stable tie-breaker. It does not turn a due date into a UTC time and contains no payment authorization. The resulting list is immutable to reduce unexpected effects between interface components.

The example assumes valid dates received through the contract; the simplified constructor does not validate the calendar. In Flutter, the screen would still need accessible semantics, understandable groups, and loading or refresh states. This is a teaching proposal in Dart, not an executed implementation. The Python lab tests scheduling and sending logic, not this widget or mobile model.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Persist the reminder’s intention, not just a time

blocks.text: A reminder job needs a reference to the obligation, its version, its purpose, and the policy that produced the instant. Storing only “send at nine” makes it difficult to know whether the work remains valid after a due-date change. I would propose an identity composed of obligation, version, and reminder type, with a separate delivery-outcome record. Confirmation of sending does not change the bill’s financial state.

Changing a time preference requires a policy for jobs already created. Recalculating them may be correct if it does not duplicate a previously accepted reminder. Ignoring them until the next cycle may be surprising. The choice should be explained to customers when relevant and applied with a configuration generation. The lab simplifies this dimension by receiving the time at dispatch; a persistent implementation would need versioned preferences and replanning.

A due date may also carry a source and confidence level. Information entered manually, detected automatically, or updated by a partner should not be indistinguishable during an investigation. The interface need not display every technical detail, but the system should preserve them. This makes discrepancies explainable without blaming customers for information that changed after entry, and without promising that a schedule replaces checking the billing document.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Before sending, check whether the job still makes sense

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The dispatcher rejects clocks without a time zone, compares versions, and checks whether the bill has already been paid. It then calculates the eligible instant and recognizes a repeated reminder. In the model, a job arriving on a different civil date expires, avoiding urgency messaging that has lost its context.

The sent set remains in memory, so the demonstrated deduplication does not survive a restart or guarantee a single effect at an external provider. For production, I would persist the decision and address the gap between external acceptance and local confirmation. The test isolates temporal semantics so this limitation remains visible rather than being hidden by infrastructure.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: The calendar belongs in the test suite

blocks.code:
def test_orders_across_month_boundaries(self):
    self.p.upsert("a", date(2026, 10, 31), 999, 1)
    self.assertEqual([key for key, _ in self.p.upcoming()], ["a", "b"])

def test_paid_before_dispatch_suppresses_reminder(self):
    self.p.upsert("b", date(2026, 11, 1), 1234, 2, paid=True)
    self.assertEqual(self.p.dispatch(
        "b", 1, datetime(2026, 11, 1, 12, tzinfo=UTC)),
                     "obsolete")
    self.assertEqual(self.p.upcoming(), [])

def test_gap_advances_to_first_valid_minute(self):
    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    value = local_instant(date(2026, 3, 29), 2, 30, zone)
    self.assertEqual(value.astimezone(zone).strftime("%H:%M"), "03:00")

def test_fold_selects_first_occurrence(self):
    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    value = local_instant(date(2026, 10, 25), 2, 30, zone)
    self.assertEqual(value, datetime(2026, 10, 25, 0, 30, tzinfo=UTC))
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The tests check a list spanning months, a payment observed before sending, and both forms of temporal ambiguity: a nonexistent time and a repeated time. Dates were selected as fixtures and have no connection to customer bills. The expected result makes the calendar policy reviewable.

The file passed nine tests, covering an invalid version, deduplication, expiration of a delayed reminder, and rejection of a clock without a zone. There was no integration with a banking calendar or DDA. In a real delivery, holidays, document rules, and differences between the due date and clearing would require additional contracts and tests without silently changing the date visible to the customer.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Measure the task of finding the next obligation

blocks.text: The primary experience metric would be success in identifying the next relevant bill with the correct amount and due date. I would measure time and interpretation errors on concrete tasks, including month changes and no bills in the current period. Fewer clicks are useful only if the person still understands what they are seeing. A shortcut that reduces navigation but increases due-date confusion does not meet the objective.

Operationally, I would separate planned, sent, update-suppressed, repeated, and delay-expired jobs. More suppressions because of payment may be positive; more expirations may indicate queue delay. Job age and the difference between planned and actual dispatch times help locate the problem. I would also observe messages sent outside preferences, classified by reason, without using personal identifiers as labels.

The effect on late payments requires causal care. People may pay late because of insufficient funds, their own choices, or incorrect information, not merely because they forgot the due date. An experiment should distinguish those conditions before assigning economic value to the assistant. The initial proposal can be validated through organization and comprehension, leaving reduced fees or delinquency as hypotheses to measure rather than promises derived from a visual improvement.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: Separate visual migration from scheduling changes

blocks.text: I would first launch the chronological view using the same known obligations while preserving access to month views and details. Research would compare the task of finding the next obligation, not merely aesthetic preference. People with many bills, recurring bills, and bills spread across months would need to participate in validation. The new presentation must not change existing due dates, amounts, or authorizations.

Reminder changes would have a separate rollout. Before sending, the candidate planner would produce decisions in comparison mode to check time, zone, and suppression after payment. The team would review cases where the candidate differs from existing behavior without overwhelming customers with two message versions. A controlled cohort would make inappropriate timing and repeat contacts measurable, with message limits and a clear stop mechanism.

Rollback would preserve delivery records and obligation versions. Reverting the scheduler must not make the backlog reappear as new work. Customer-selected preferences must also remain in force even if the previous presentation lacks some controls. The migration plan would include read compatibility and support guidance explaining why a reminder was sent, suppressed, or expired at each stage.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: A useful schedule must remain readable under pressure

blocks.text: People may check due dates while commuting, working, or experiencing poor connectivity. I would prioritize amount, date, and state, keeping charts and secondary explanations from competing with the immediate decision. A sorted list must preserve context when it updates: if a bill disappears because it was marked paid, the interface must avoid shifting focus so that the next action lands on another item without the user noticing.

For accessibility, relative and absolute dates can complement each other. “Tomorrow” is quick to read, while an explicit date prevents ambiguity when revisiting a screenshot or delayed message. Urgency colors need equivalent text, and amounts should be announced understandably. A glass-and-transparency design would be acceptable only if contrast, focus, and readability remained clear across different backgrounds and motion settings.

For performance, I would use pagination or incremental loading when volume required it while retaining a fast query for the next due date. The server can offer an ordered view, but the contract must explain filters and coverage. A partial list must not be presented as evidence that no other bills exist. The assistant’s quality depends on organization and honesty about what has loaded, not just smooth animation.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: ADR: civil dates in the domain, instants in operations

blocks.text: The proposed decision keeps due dates as civil dates and calculates notification instants using an explicit zone and preference. Storing everything as UTC timestamps simplifies some queue mechanisms but shifts a business interpretation into implicit conversions. Using only the device’s local time makes consistency harder when people change devices, travel, or go offline. I would choose a contract that preserves both representations and their purposes.

The system also needs a policy for clock transitions. The lab advances to the first valid minute and chooses the first occurrence when a time repeats. That policy is demonstrative and should be reviewed for the product. For financial reminders, predictability and avoiding duplicates matter more than an apparently elegant conversion nobody can explain to a customer or support agent.

The accepted cost is storing more context and maintaining calendar tests. The benefit is preventing time-zone changes from altering the meaning of a due date. I would revisit the ADR if the app expanded to more countries, obligations had specific contractual times, or preferences needed to follow travel automatically. These changes require product and data decisions, not merely switching date libraries.

pages.chapter_title: The next due date, without searching across months

pages.title: EM: deliver organization, not a collection of features

blocks.text: As an EM, I would define the main task with product and research: recognize the next obligation and know which action is available. I would then separate the query delivery, reminder review, and any payment evolution. This reduces dependencies and prevents an organizational improvement from becoming a broad automation project without a clear hypothesis. Support would contribute contact reasons and examples of misinterpretation.

As a Staff engineer, I would review the temporal model, obligation identity, and job revalidation. Technical discussions would include queue failures, payments observed after scheduling, and preferences changed during the wait. The lab’s nine tests serve as executable examples of those decisions. For a real implementation, I would add persistence and integration tests only after settling the semantics, rather than using infrastructure to hide unanswered domain questions.

Initial value would be time saved per planning session and fewer contacts about locating bills or reminder timing. Financial benefits associated with late payments would require causal measurement. My interview question would be: “When an obligation changes between planning and notification, which version has authority, and how does the customer perceive that change?” The answer connects calendars, consistency, experience, and responsible execution.
