chapters.title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task
chapters.subtitle: From public evidence to a verifiable contract
chapters.source_title: Google Play — Fernando Cordeiro review about viewing the statement

pages.title: 09 · Preserve the task during visual evolution

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.

blocks.text: A public review questions changes to the statement view, including the relationship between hiding a chart, seeing the total, and navigating between months. The cited version has not been independently reproduced. The signal raises a product question: which information must remain available regardless of a presentation preference? This chapter turns that question into verifiable contracts without asserting a current defect in the app.

A statement is a financial view with established expectations. People return to find the amount, due date, and transactions, compare periods, and understand situations such as partial payment or a reversal. An interface can gain visual consistency while increasing the effort required for these tasks. Risk arises when the implementation makes essential data depend on the presence of a decorative component.

I would investigate tasks before choosing a new layout. I would observe regular users, including people using screen readers, enlarged text, and unstable connections. I would distinguish aesthetic preference from interpretation errors: both matter, but require different responses. The technical proposal keeps the financial snapshot, period selection, and visual preferences in separate states. The lab demonstrates that separation with synthetic data; real validation would need statement rules, research, and the components actually used.

sources.title: Google Play — Fernando Cordeiro review about viewing the statement

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: Three states, three responsibilities

blocks.text: The first state is financial: period, revision, total, due date, and transactions in a coherent snapshot. The second is navigation: which period the person selected and which query is in progress. The third is presentation: chart visibility, sorting, or section expansion. Mixing them creates accidental dependencies, such as hiding the total when a visual preference is disabled or replacing the current month when an old response arrives.

In the lab, Invoice requires a tuple of entries, validates integer cents, and checks the sum. Rejecting mutable lists preserves the snapshot after validation. This equality is a local simplification, not the complete formula for a real statement. Fees, payments, and adjustments would need explicit entries or another reconcilable contract. A revision identifies content; two responses with the same revision and different due dates are a conflict, not an innocent update.

Month selection is explicit. A response for another period cannot silently be applied to the screen. When the user changes months, the controller retains navigation intent and associates the response with the relevant request. Preferences can survive the change, but do not alter the snapshot. This design helps test empty, delayed, and conflicting states without requiring a complete visual test for every domain rule.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: Financial data and preferences stay separate
pages.kicker: PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · NOT AN INTERNAL DESIGN

blocks.title: Financial data and preferences stay separate
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture. Boxes represent responsibilities; arrows make contracts explicit.

blocks.text: The proposal keeps the essential summary outside the condition that determines whether the chart renders. The controller associates each response with the requested period and prevents a delayed response from changing the selected context. A cache can improve opening time, provided it indicates freshness and never presents an old revision as confirmation of a recent payment.

The design does not give the client authority to calculate the debt. Local validation checks the consistency of a synthetic contract; in production, the financial source defines field semantics. Separating preferences allows visualization changes without migrating financial data. It also reduces impossible states: a chart can be hidden while the total and due date remain visible. The central architectural test is to trace an interaction to the dependency it modifies. If hiding a component changes the snapshot, the boundary is wrong or requires explicit product justification.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: A controller that rejects inconsistent responses

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_09.py. Executed local Python model; not an app implementation.

blocks.text: The lab excerpt applies revisions only to the currently selected period. A lower revision is ignored; an equal revision with different content is rejected. The chart preference affects only the projection's chart field. Total and due date derive from the snapshot, preserving the primary task when the chart is hidden.

The model includes neither asynchronous networking nor persistence across sessions. In a real application, the controller would need request identity, logical cancellation, and loading states. The exercise makes explicit the conditions that any state-management mechanism should preserve, regardless of the chosen library.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: Flutter: the summary exists without the chart

blocks.caption: Educational Flutter/Dart excerpt, not executed. Independent component with no dependency on internal NuDS.

blocks.text: The Flutter example highlights the presentation boundary: showChart controls only the supplementary visual. Formatted values are component inputs; their source and authorization sit outside this tree. The Semantics widget provides structural information, but does not replace real evaluation with assistive technologies or independently solve contrast, focus, and navigation order.

A complete integration would need approved components and tokens, currency localization, and handling of unavailable values. I would avoid replacing absence with zero, because that communicates a different financial situation. The excerpt is illustrative and was not compiled in this environment; only the associated Python lab was executed.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: A snapshot contract, not a sum calculated on screen

blocks.caption: Proposed JSON contract with synthetic data; only the Invoice subset is executed in the lab.

blocks.text: The proposed contract makes currency, period, revision, and completeness explicit. Negative values represent adjustments in this example; they are not validation errors by definition. A real API would need to specify exactly which components enter the total and how installments, payments, fees, and reversals are reflected. The client should not reconstruct an incomplete financial rule from partially loaded entries.

The complete field distinguishes a full list from a results page, but trusting it requires an authorized producer. The lab uses a complete tuple to check consistency. This JSON adds documentation of intent and does not claim to describe Nubank's format.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: The race between months needs a defined response

blocks.text: Imagine two queries: someone opens October and selects September before the response arrives. September's response arrives first; October follows. A controller that applies any response to the current state changes the month without consent. Canceling the earlier request can save resources, but is not a sufficient guarantee: it may have finished or passed through a cache. The application rule must check the current intent.

Another race involves revisions. A payment or adjustment changes the snapshot while the app reads the period. Mixing a total from one revision with entries from another creates an inconsistency perceived as a financial error. The solution might be a complete snapshot, a read token, or a pagination contract tied to a revision. The mechanism depends on the source; the principle is not to combine data without knowing whether they belong to the same state.

Presentation failures deserve their own states. Truncated text, missing currency, and loading that erases the total are different experiences from an unavailable statement. I would preserve useful context during refresh and identify when it is older. I would neither show zero for a failed query nor hide the period to save space. Customers need to know what they are seeing and whether the information is ready to support a decision.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: The important assertion is not that the chart exists

blocks.caption: Excerpt from labs/case_09.py. Local result: 8 tests passed; see results_09.txt.

blocks.text: Eight tests passed in the complete lab. The excerpt verifies independence from visual preference, an empty month, a signed adjustment, and a delayed revision. The others reject an inconsistent snapshot, a revision conflict, the wrong period, and entries in a mutable list. The last barrier prevents content from changing after validation. The properties examined are semantic.

This does not replace widget tests. They would need to confirm that the tree actually exposes the total, enlarged text remains usable, and month navigation is operable. The combination is valuable: fast rules isolate the domain, while interface evaluations verify how it translates into the experience.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: Measure understanding, not just screen opens

blocks.text: Statement opens can increase when the experience gets worse: people return repeatedly to confirm the same amount. I would therefore not use views as the primary success metric. Measurement would begin with tasks: finding the total and due date, identifying the period, locating a transaction, and explaining statement status. Moderated research helps reveal errors that click events cannot.

In telemetry, I would collect completed navigation and loading failures with app revision, text size, and device class where permitted. I would not record financial amounts in analytics events to answer questions that can be measured in aggregate. Repeated period changes may indicate legitimate exploration; they need context before being labeled friction.

The health dashboard would combine snapshot inconsistencies, responses discarded because of context, read latency, and categorized contacts about comprehension. I would segment by accessibility usage and connection without assuming an average represents everyone. Better speed accompanied by more errors identifying the due date would be a regression. The team needs a comprehension metric and a harm guardrail, as well as the ability to inspect consented examples when the numbers conflict.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: A visual migration also requires compatibility

blocks.text: Rollout begins with an inventory of tasks and states in the previous experience. Listing replaced components is insufficient. We need to know how a regular user finds previous months, recognizes a reversal, and resumes an interrupted query. The migration preserves those outcomes or offers a clearly better path validated with real people. A new design pattern alone does not demonstrate reduced effort.

I would separate changes to content, behavior, and style so the experiment remains interpretable. Changing monthly navigation, the chart, and total hierarchy simultaneously makes a decline in completion difficult to attribute. The first cohort would include diverse devices and access needs, with a defined rollback path. Local settings must remain valid; an old preference should not accidentally hide a new essential component.

Before expanding, I would review quantitative metrics alongside research observations and support contacts. An inconclusive result does not justify expansion merely because there were no crashes. Rollback should restore an experience compatible with current data without switching the financial source or deleting preferences. If maintaining variants becomes costly, I would set a decision window and explicit closure criteria, avoiding a permanent experiment nobody can operate.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: Accessibility is financial semantics

blocks.text: An accessible tree must communicate more than visible text. Total, due date, period, and status need understandable structure and order. A button announced only as arrow does not explain whether it changes the month or expands a section. Focus should not jump to the beginning when an update arrives or disappear when the chart is hidden. These properties require tests on real devices and assistive technologies.

Enlarged text changes composition. Shrinking the font to fit is not the solution: layout must reflow, prioritize information, and avoid fixed heights for variable content. I would also check the distinction between positive amounts, negative adjustments, and unavailable states. Color can reinforce meaning, but must not be the only way to communicate debt, credit, or error. Currency formatting must keep sign and unit identifiable.

Security includes presentation privacy. Screenshots, previews, and error records can expose statement data if the team treats the screen as ordinary content. Telemetry should minimize those data and prevent exceptions from printing the entire snapshot. The goal is to preserve autonomy without turning observability into a parallel repository of financial information. This connects visual quality, semantics, and engineering discipline within a single product review.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: ADR 09 · A financial snapshot independent of visuals

blocks.text: The decision is to model financial information as an immutable snapshot, keeping navigation and preferences in separate states. The context is an evolving interface that receives asynchronous responses and must preserve familiar tasks. The main benefit is not a specific library: it is fewer invalid states and predictable boundaries around which interaction can change which part of the experience.

One alternative is a single mutable object containing data, loading, and presentation fields. It simplifies the beginning but allows meaningless combinations: a new month with an old total, a hidden chart with no summary, a current revision with an earlier list. Another alternative is to derive the entire statement from visible transactions. That would be correct only if the contract guaranteed completeness and fully represented the financial rule—conditions a screen should not assume.

Separation requires an explicit controller and compatibility tests between snapshots and components. It also requires deciding how to display older information during refresh. I would record that policy as part of the experience contract, not leave it as a detail for each screen. I would reconsider the design if the source cannot supply a coherent revision or pagination prevents validating the whole. In that case, the right change is to strengthen the contract, not hide discrepancies behind more complex visual states.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

pages.title: EM execution: protect understanding through change

blocks.text: As Engineering Manager, I would establish a short initiative with Design, Research, Mobile, and statement owners. The first delivery would be agreement on essential tasks and financial states, backed by verifiable examples. I would distribute ownership across the data contract, behavior, and accessibility, avoiding reliance on one reviewer who knows the old experience. Planning would include regular users and time to address findings.

Value would begin with comprehension and effort: completed queries, time to find information, and demonstrated reduction in repeat contacts. To express support impact as operational value, I would use eligible volume, causal change, and an appropriate unit cost. I would not present fewer clicks as revenue. I would also track migration cost and temporary variant maintenance. A simple change can be a better investment than rebuilding the entire experience.

The Staff question would be: which invariant remains true when a customer toggles the chart, month, and text size while responses arrive out of order? The answer must connect domain, state, and rendering. The leadership question would be who stops expansion when the average improves but a relevant group loses the ability to understand the statement. That decision must be agreed before the experiment, with clear evidence and responsibilities.

pages.chapter_title: Evolve the statement without losing the primary task

lab.scope: Local immutable projection and eight tests; no complete statement calculation or real app.

chapters.title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning
chapters.subtitle: From public evidence to a verifiable contract
chapters.source_title: Google Play — Neidslem Fernandes da Costa review about purchase records

pages.title: 10 · Define the right document first

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.

blocks.text: A public review asks to share proof of a credit-card purchase without depending on email support. The need is understandable, but the source does not clarify which document would resolve the situation. A purchase record, confirmation of statement payment, and a merchant document are not equivalent. Creating a button before resolving this ambiguity could simply accelerate sending inappropriate information.

The investigation would begin with reasons for requesting the document. Does the person want to acknowledge a purchase, dispute a charge, request reimbursement, or demonstrate payment? Each purpose requires different fields, language, and responsibility. I would review anonymized examples with support and product owners, separating requests eligible for self-service from situations that still require assistance. The sample should not include only documents that are easy to generate.

This chapter proposes a versioned, shareable record associated with the known transaction state. It states its scope and minimizes unnecessary data. The lab produces this record from an immutable object, checks synthetic authorization, and detects content changes using a local secret. It does not create a tax receipt, confirm external settlement, or replace a legally valid signature. Its contribution is to show that semantics, access, and integrity must be designed together before discussing appearance or file format.

sources.title: Google Play — Neidslem Fernandes da Costa review about purchase records

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Authorized, confirmed, and reversed are not synonyms

blocks.text: The document domain begins with the purchase lifecycle. A pending authorization may reserve capacity without representing the same situation as a confirmed purchase. A later reversal changes the record's meaning, but should not erase the fact that an earlier version was issued. The experience must state the status and reference date, avoiding a generic paid label when available information does not support it.

In the lab, Purchase contains an identifier, owner, revision, amount, merchant, and state. A closed set of labels translates the three synthetic states. The revision changes when relevant content changes. The document receives a snapshot copy rather than querying fields individually during assembly. This prevents mixing an amount from one revision with a status from another. A complete real-card rule would require a richer vocabulary.

An issued document and a current document are different objects. A shared file may continue to exist after a reversal, so copies already distributed cannot be promised automatic updates. A verifiable reference can provide the latest status, provided it does not expose data to unauthorized third parties. The product decision must explain that limitation. Customers need to know whether they are sending a historical snapshot or a live query, and recipients must be able to interpret its scope.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Export an authorized snapshot
pages.kicker: PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · NOT AN INTERNAL DESIGN

blocks.title: Export an authorized snapshot
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture. Boxes represent responsibilities; arrows make contracts explicit.

blocks.text: Authorization belongs to object access, not merely to the existence of a session. The generator receives a coherent snapshot and applies a field allowlist. It does not automatically copy all source data into the document. The artifact is immutable; another revision produces another record and preserves the relationship between them.

The verification arrow is optional and requires a privacy decision. Making a public identifier queryable can turn convenience into exposure of financial activity. External verification could confirm only integrity and version, without returning the full history. The lab uses a local HMAC to detect tampering but does not implement public verification infrastructure. The architecture separates these responsibilities so that choosing PDF or an image does not conceal important decisions about access, temporal validity, and the meaning of what is shared.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: An explicit allowlist of shareable fields

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_10.py. Local HMAC with a test key; neither a legally valid signature nor real infrastructure.

blocks.text: The executed generator compares the owner with the supplied subject and rejects invalid states or amounts. The document is assembled field by field; owner is not exported. The notice accompanies the content to prevent the record being mistaken for statement settlement or a tax receipt. The integrity tag covers the canonical body.

The subject and secret are controlled test inputs, not production authentication mechanisms. A real service would need trusted sources for both, key management, and consistent authorization. The example demonstrates content minimization and state preservation without claiming complete sharing security.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Clojure: contract before rendering

blocks.code:
(ns portfolio.purchase-record)

(def labels
  {:pending "Autorização pendente"
   :confirmed "Registro de compra confirmada"
   :reversed "Compra estornada"})

(defn public-record [purchase subject]
  (when-not (= subject (:owner purchase))
    (throw (ex-info "Forbidden" {:kind :forbidden})))
  (let [status (:status purchase)
        label (get labels status)]
    (when-not label
      (throw (ex-info "Unsupported state"
                      {:kind :invalid-state})))
    (assoc
      (select-keys purchase
        [:purchase-id :revision :amount-cents
         :merchant :status])
      :label label
      :kind :purchase-record
      :notice "Não comprova quitação da fatura")))

;; Proposta pura: autenticação e assinatura são externas.
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure excerpt, not executed; names and contracts proposed by the author.

blocks.text: This educational function expresses the same boundary in Clojure: verify object access and select fields before rendering. A visual template receives only the public model, reducing the risk of accidentally including internal information. Complete type and value handling would still be necessary; the excerpt emphasizes access and semantics alone.

The contract is independently authored and does not correspond to a known Nubank API. A pure function allows the transformation to be reviewed separately from PDF, storage, and transport. If the public model is wrong, changing the renderer does not fix it; it distributes the same incorrect interpretation in another form.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Persist the artifact's revision and purpose

blocks.code:
-- Esquema proposto; não executado pelo laboratório.
CREATE TABLE purchase_records (
  document_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  purchase_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  purchase_revision BIGINT NOT NULL,
  template_revision INTEGER NOT NULL,
  document_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  state_at_issue TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload_digest TEXT NOT NULL,
  storage_reference TEXT NOT NULL,
  issued_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  owner_reference TEXT NOT NULL,

-- Acesso ao blob ainda exige autorização.
-- Digest não torna o arquivo anônimo ou público.
blocks.caption: Proposed reference SQL. Not executed; the lab uses immutable Python objects.

blocks.text: The schema is a proposed option for storing artifact metadata, not a description of Nubank's persistence. Identity combines purchase revision, template revision, and document type. A visual change can therefore produce a different file without pretending the transaction changed. The storage reference must not be treated as a permanent public URL.

An implementation would need decisions on retention, encryption, access policy, and reconciliation between the record and blob. The lab keeps only in-memory objects and does not execute this SQL. This distinction prevents a small exercise from being used as proof of durable or secure document distribution.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: A reversal can happen while the file is being generated

blocks.text: The main race is between reading the purchase and issuing the document. If the state changes during generation, canceling the file is not necessarily correct: it may represent a valid historical snapshot. What must not happen is mixing fields from different revisions or omitting the temporal reference. The decision depends on the document's purpose and must be communicated before sharing.

Another failure occurs after generation. The file exists, but the customer loses the response and retries. A key based on purchase, revision, template, and purpose can return the same artifact, avoiding duplicate cost and indistinguishable versions. Sharing remains an explicit device action; generating a file does not authorize sending it to a previously used recipient. These are different consents and effects.

There are also integrity and access failures. A valid tag does not mean the requester may read the object. An expired link should not leak metadata to explain the error. A defective template can produce an incorrect document with a correct hash, because integrity only shows that the bytes have not changed. Tests must therefore examine meaning, authorization, and rendering as well as cryptographic verification. None of these layers replaces the others.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Tests distinguish integrity from meaning

blocks.caption: Excerpt from labs/case_10.py. Result: 7 tests passed; see results_10.txt.

blocks.text: Seven tests passed in the complete lab. The excerpt checks labels, revision, minimization, denied access, and determinism for the same snapshot. The remaining tests alter the amount after issuance and verify rejection of unsuitable values. A document can retain integrity while being inappropriate for its purpose, which is why labels are also asserted.

The tests do not validate authentication, secret management, or interpretation by third parties. For a pilot, I would add content review with Product and Legal, samples of installment purchases and reversals, and evaluation of document reading outside the app. External context changes what must be explicit.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Self-service that resolves needs, not just generates files

blocks.text: Counting downloads is insufficient to evaluate the product. Someone may download three documents because none meets the need. I would carefully measure the declared or inferred reason, successful generation, and subsequent contact about the same purchase. The goal is to determine whether the record replaces an eligible support request without pushing uncertainty to another channel.

For technical health, I would track failures by stage: authorization, reading, rendering, storage, and delivery. This separates unavailability from denied access and reveals templates that fail on specific content. A correlation identifier should link the request to stages without placing the entire document in logs. Amounts, merchants, and names are not necessary for every operational metric.

Quality requires sampling issued documents under appropriate access controls and purpose. The dashboard should highlight incorrect states, missing revisions, and discrepancies between artifact and source. I would also track cost per issuance and artifact reuse rate. Greater efficiency with semantically confusing documents is not success. Support needs a way to record that a customer received a file but still lacked suitable evidence for the situation that prompted the request.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Launch by purpose, then broaden coverage

blocks.text: The first pilot should choose a narrow purpose and a well-understood set of states. For example, it could provide a confirmed-purchase record for reference and informational sharing, with reviewed wording. Covering every situation initially creates an overly broad implicit contract and obscures which documents actually resolve requests. The initial restriction must be clear to customers and support.

Before exposure, I would compare generated examples with information currently provided by support, investigating differences in semantics and content. The team would test the full experience of obtaining the file, opening it on another device, and understanding its limits. People receiving it outside the app lack the context of the previous screen. The file must carry sufficient information without accumulating unnecessary personal data.

Expansion would be guided by resolution and repeat contact, with sampling of problematic cases. Disabling the button prevents new issuance but does not retrieve files already shared; that consequence belongs in the risk plan. Template revisions must be traceable, and communicating corrections requires an appropriate process. The feature flag controls future exposure; document governance addresses what has already been issued. Treating them as the same leaves an important part of the journey without an owner.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: Sharing creates a new privacy boundary

blocks.text: Inside the app, access may depend on session and authorization. After sharing, the file can circulate beyond the original intent. The proposal minimizes information during generation: no full card number, secret, or internal identifier automatically enters the public model. Field selection must match the document's purpose, not the convenience of reusing an API object.

Verifiable links require additional care. A long token can reduce guessing, but remains a credential if it grants content access. Expiration, revocation, scope, and usage records must be designed for the case. A public page confirming a purchase exists can disclose information even without displaying an amount. Verification must separate integrity evidence from querying current financial state.

The lab HMAC uses a fixed test secret to make tampering observable. This is not production key management, a public signature, or legal validity. A real service would need rotation, secure storage, environment separation, and permission review. Malicious content in merchant names would also need testing to prevent renderer problems. Document security spans data, representation, and distribution; it does not end with selecting a cryptographic algorithm.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: ADR 10 · Issue a verifiable purchase snapshot

blocks.text: The proposed decision is to issue an immutable snapshot with explicit state, revision, and purpose. The context is a self-service demand whose meaning varies between customers. The objective is to reduce support dependence for eligible requests without calling every record proof of payment. The public model is separate from the internal object and precedes the visual format decision.

One alternative is to export the screen directly. This preserves a familiar appearance, but may include unnecessary information, omit temporal context, and depend on device size. Another is to always generate a document with the latest data and no revision reference. That simplifies current reading but complicates explaining what someone shared before a reversal. An explicit snapshot offers traceability at the cost of retention and clear communication about updates.

I would reconsider the decision if the dominant purpose requires a document from another participant, such as the merchant, or if an informational record does not reduce repeat contact. The better product might then guide people toward the correct request rather than create more formats. I would also record that cryptographic integrity does not establish the commercial truth of the content. Architecture guarantees association with a source and revision; the domain remains responsible for the issued document's meaning and legitimacy.

pages.chapter_title: A purchase record in context, with the right meaning

pages.title: EM execution: correct language prevents rework

blocks.text: As Engineering Manager, I would bring together Cards, Support, Design, and those responsible for document interpretation. The first decision would name the purpose and delimit covered states with approved examples. Technical work would then have concrete acceptance criteria: a coherent source, object-level authorization, minimization, traceability, and comprehension outside the app. I would avoid splitting the team into PDF generation and button creation before that alignment.

The value model would use eligible requests, effective adoption, resolution without repeat contact, and incremental cost per contact. It would deduct issuance, storage, maintenance, and investigation of problematic documents. A download is not an avoided support interaction, and freed capacity does not automatically become financial savings. The pilot must show that people achieve their purpose, not merely export a file.

The Staff question would be: what remains true when a purchase is reversed between generation, download, and the recipient reading it? The answer must separate historical snapshot, current state, and query authorization. The leadership question would be who responds when a document is intact but fails its expected purpose. A mature team does not use successful generation to close a product problem. It observes the outcome and adjusts the promise made to the customer.

chapters.title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed
chapters.subtitle: From public evidence to a verifiable contract
chapters.source_title: How we reduced critical path latency by 76% at Nubank

pages.title: 11 · The published result is a starting point

blocks.caption: Original official publication, accessed 23 October 2026.

blocks.text: Nubank published a case reducing the P90 of a payment-conditions API from approximately 1,200 to 280 milliseconds. The account describes local improvements followed by event-based aggregation with persisted reads and fallback. That result belongs to the documented flow and period; it is neither the latency of the entire app nor a gain delivered by this portfolio.

The independent contribution begins with the next question: what criteria identify another read suitable for materialization? The answer must combine composition cost, dependency variability, and explicit tolerance for stale data. Observing a slow query is insufficient. A condition shown to a customer may tolerate a snapshot briefly, while financial authorization requires validation at another boundary.

I would begin with tracing, redundant-call identification, and latency distribution by dependency. I would propose new persistence only after exhausting simple changes and understanding data semantics. This chapter's lab models versioned components, freshness budgets, and fallback. It neither measures performance nor executes payments. Its purpose is to make a read decision verifiable: when the projection may be used and when it must yield to the source, without hiding the operational cost transferred to event processing.

sources.title: How we reduced critical path latency by 76% at Nubank

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Freshness is a contract per component

blocks.text: A composite projection combines data that can change at different rates. A single update timestamp can conceal that only one component was refreshed. The synthetic model therefore tracks version and observed time separately for balance and limit. A read uses the projection only when both are present and within the configured budget. Choosing that budget belongs to the domain, not the cache alone.

Version and time answer different questions. Version prevents an older update from replacing a newer one; time helps assess age. A recently transported event can carry old state, and a future clock can make data appear fresh indefinitely. The lab rejects future timestamps relative to the clock supplied by the test. A distributed deployment would need defined time sources and clock-skew tolerance.

Completeness must also be distinguished from validity. Having every field does not mean those fields may authorize an operation. The projection may serve an estimate or presentation condition while confirmation queries the responsible service. The contract must make this distinction explicit so another team does not reuse a fast read as financial authority. A fast interface creates incentives for broader usage; documented, verifiable limits prevent convenience from becoming dangerous coupling.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Complexity moves from reads into updates
pages.kicker: PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · NOT AN INTERNAL DESIGN

blocks.title: Complexity moves from reads into updates
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture. Boxes represent responsibilities; arrows make contracts explicit.

blocks.text: The proposed architecture favors predictable reads but adds an update system that must be operated. A consumer can lag, receive duplicate events, or rebuild a projection. The API must not interpret projection-store availability as proof of freshness: the read contract checks completeness and age for each relevant component.

Fallback preserves a correctness path but can receive a traffic surge when the projection fails. Capacity, concurrency limits, and fallback priority therefore belong in the initial design. The arrow to the customer carries conditions with defined meaning; it does not transfer financial authorization authority. The lab uses local functions to represent these boundaries. A real proposal would require observability, degradation policies, and domain contracts. Materialization is worthwhile only when the new operational cost is justified by the variability removed from the critical path.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Apply a version without accepting a regression

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_11.py. Executed Python; synthetic projection without financial authorization.

blocks.text: This executed core receives a component, version, value, and time. Older updates are ignored; a repeated version with different content raises a conflict. Comparison does not depend on time alone, because transport and clocks do not independently establish business order. The component set is closed to keep the contract inspectable.

Storage is in memory and does not demonstrate atomicity across processes. In production, comparison and update would need a consistent boundary with defined recovery and reprocessing. The excerpt supports discussion of version semantics before choosing Datomic, DynamoDB, or another persistence mechanism.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Clojure: a read with an explicit alternative path

blocks.code:
(ns portfolio.conditions)

(def required-components #{:balance :limit})

(defn fresh? [now max-age parts]
  (and
    (every? #(contains? parts %) required-components)
    (every?
      (fn [{:keys [observed-at]}]
        (<= 0 (- now observed-at) max-age))
      (vals parts))))

(defn read-conditions
  [projection now max-age canonical-reader]
  (if (fresh? now max-age projection)
    {:source :projection
     :purpose :display-conditions
     :data projection}
    {:source :canonical
     :purpose :display-conditions
     :data (canonical-reader)}))

;; canonical-reader é contrato proposto, não API do Nu.
;; Autorizar pagamento pertence a outra fronteira.
blocks.caption: Proposed Clojure excerpt, not executed; canonical-reader is an independent abstract dependency.

blocks.text: The function receives the canonical reader as an explicit dependency. This makes path selection testable without opening a real connection. The response carries source and purpose to aid diagnosis, but metadata does not replace access discipline. A consumer should not treat the declared purpose as authorization to bypass financial validation.

The excerpt is educational and includes no timeout, bulkhead, concurrency limit, or canonical-path failure handling. Those controls are needed so a projection failure does not take down the source. The design must specify behavior when both paths are unavailable, keeping the customer response honest.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Kafka transports a versioned fact, not a global guarantee

blocks.caption: Independently proposed envelope and topic name. Not executed in Kafka; the lab uses local calls.

blocks.text: The proposed envelope retains domain identity and version even when transport provides partition ordering. Different partitions, reprocessing, and consumers writing to external storage still require their own rules. Producer configuration must not become a promise of a single end-to-end effect.

The partition key is a distribution and affinity choice with consequences for volume and hotspots. The example contains no real data and creates no topic. The purpose field documents the contract; it is not sufficient security control. Deployment would require a compatible schema, permissions, retention, and a verifiable projection-rebuild plan.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Fallback can become the next failure

blocks.text: An unavailable projection immediately changes load distribution. If all reads switch to the source simultaneously, the mechanism intended to protect correctness can saturate it and worsen the outage. The design must consider contingency capacity, prioritization, and concurrency limits. The correct response to excess load may be an explicit wait, not unlimited retries across multiple layers.

Late events create another failure category. Storage responds quickly, but content is stale. HTTP success rate can remain excellent while the experience uses unsuitable information. Freshness checks must be in the read path with component-specific criteria. Policy must also define what happens when time is untrustworthy or the source publishes no heartbeat for unchanged state.

Rebuilding deserves first-class treatment. Reprocessing history with new logic can produce results different from existing projections. I would compare parallel projections and record discrepancies before switching traffic. Older updates must not overwrite newer data during backfill. The solution may involve revision namespaces and a promotion barrier. These mechanisms add complexity, but make the true cost of removing synchronous composition from the critical path explicit.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Freshness tests, not a latency benchmark

blocks.code:
def test_fresh_projection_used(self):
    result = self.view.read(105, 10, self.origin)
    self.assertEqual(result['source'], 'projection')

def test_old_component_forces_fallback(self):
    self.view.apply('balance', 2, 900, 119, 119)
    result = self.view.read(120, 10, self.origin)
    self.assertEqual(result['source'], 'canonical')
    self.assertEqual(self.view.fallbacks, 1)

def test_old_version_does_not_replace(self):
    self.view.apply('balance', 2, 900, 101, 101)
    self.assertFalse(self.view.apply('balance', 1, 1000, 100, 101))
    self.assertEqual(self.view.parts['balance'][0], 2)

def test_conflicting_version_rejected(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.view.apply('limit', 1, 3000, 100, 100)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from labs/case_11.py. Result: 7 tests passed; see results_11.txt. No benchmark.

blocks.text: All seven local tests passed. The excerpt verifies selection of a fresh projection, fallback for a stale component, and rejection of version regression. Other tests cover conflicting content at the same version, future timestamps, missing components, and explicit unavailability. The clock is an input, allowing boundaries to be examined without waiting in real time.

No result measures milliseconds or reproduces Nubank's published gain. Performance evaluation would require representative load, dependency distributions, and tail observation. The lab demonstrates only local read decisions. This separation protects the material's credibility: a functional property can be correct even when the architecture has not yet demonstrated economic benefit.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Observe writes to trust reads

blocks.text: The read dashboard must show latency and response source, but that is only half the story. Projection health depends on consumer lag, completeness, component age, and divergence from the source. I would avoid a single cache-hit indicator: a high rate can mean efficiency or persistent use of unsuitable content, depending on the freshness contract.

Tail metrics must be segmented by path. Combining materialized reads and fallback can conceal degradation of the latter until it receives more traffic. I would also track fallback frequency and reason, version conflicts, and rebuild time. Individual identifiers belong in access-controlled traces, not metric labels that unnecessarily multiply cardinality.

The business objective is journey completion with correct conditions and acceptable waiting. Improved P90 accompanied by more discrepancies or confirmation failures is not a win. I would define guardrails before rollout and maintain sampled comparison. Alerts must distinguish delayed transport, a silent producer, and an unavailable source because each requires a different action. Operating a fast read means understanding the path that feeds it, not merely the database that responds.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Silent comparison before serving conditions

blocks.text: Deployment would start in comparison mode: build the projection and query its result on a sample without changing the customer response. Differences would be classified as expected lag, transformation errors, incomplete sources, or incompatible semantics. An aggregate equality percentage is insufficient; critical fields need their own analysis and a set of explainable examples.

After validating freshness and correctness, a small cohort could receive materialized reads. Fallback would be deliberately exercised in a controlled environment to confirm capacity and behavior. The plan would include exposure limits, pause criteria, and a return to the previous path. I would also test the inverse situation: a degraded source while the projection looks healthy, since serving stale data without a limit can conceal a meaningful problem.

Expansion depends on net benefit, not architectural preference. I would measure perceived latency, journey completion, processing cost, and operational effort. If most queries require fallback, the staleness tolerance may be too small for the chosen pattern. I would then revisit composition or the contract rather than silently relax the freshness guarantee. The experiment must be allowed to conclude that materialization is unsuitable for that flow.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: Fast financial data still need boundaries

blocks.text: The projection increases the number of places where relevant data exist. This requires explicit purpose, access, and retention. Storage designed for fast reads should not become a generic repository open to any service. Each consumer must demonstrate that its use is compatible with the offered semantics and freshness. Authorizing a payment with a presentation field would be a contract change, not a simple optimization.

For performance, the first question is where time is being spent. Reducing duplicate calls, propagating validated context, and removing layers with no domain role may be sufficient. Materialization is justified only when structural cost remains and asynchronous updates are acceptable. I would also consider object size, invalidation frequency, and traffic concentration: an overly broad projection can shift bottlenecks into writes and storage.

The lab maintains synthetic balance and limit values, without authenticated identity or customer isolation. A real implementation would need to preserve read authorization and prevent entity mixing in the aggregator. Tests would include incorrect keys, insufficient permissions, and backup restoration. Reliability and security meet at this boundary: a fast response to the wrong person is a serious failure even when version, age, and latency are within limits.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: ADR 11 · Materialize only with freshness semantics

blocks.text: The proposed decision is to materialize a composite read only when documented freshness tolerance and an operable canonical contingency path exist. The context is variability from synchronous dependencies, not a rule that caches always improve architecture. The objective is to reduce tail latency and make reads predictable while preserving the meaning of data used by the journey.

One alternative is to retain synchronous composition while optimizing calls, parallelism, and context propagation. It reduces operational state but retains dependence on service availability and tail latency. Another is a cache with a single expiry and no component versions. It is simpler, but can hide inconsistency and cannot explain which data became stale. A versioned projection offers finer control at the cost of consumption, reconciliation, backfill, and observability.

I would record abandonment conditions: a low share of eligible reads, disproportionate operational cost, or inability to define safe freshness. I would also state what is outside the decision: financial authorization mechanisms and Nubank's internal architecture are not part of this exercise. Architectural review must compare alternatives using journey data. The published result inspires a way of reasoning; it does not relieve the team of demonstrating that the same pattern fits another context.

pages.chapter_title: Fast payments without trading correctness for speed

pages.title: EM execution: distribute the new architecture's cost

blocks.text: As Engineering Manager, I would align Product, source domains, and Platform on the problem and guarantees. One team may gain latency while another inherits event load, support, and contract maintenance. Planning must recognize that transfer to avoid a local optimization that creates operational debt elsewhere. I would define owners for producers, projection, API, fallback, and reconciliation, with operational criteria before launch.

Value would be estimated from eligible attempts, causal change in completion, and margin per completion, minus infrastructure and operations. I would also measure capacity recovered through fewer calls. These components cannot be added without checking overlap. The 76% gain belongs to the official case; no lab number supports projecting revenue or availability. An investment decision requires an internal baseline and sensitivity analysis of assumptions.

The Staff question would be: how do we prove that a fast read remains acceptable when just one component stops updating and fallback receives all traffic? The answer must cover version, freshness, capacity, and failure experience. The leadership question would be who can stop rollout and which contingency cost was funded. An architecture is ready to expand only when the organization can operate it as clearly as it can draw it.

chapters.title: Cloud capacity as a product commitment
chapters.subtitle: From public evidence to a verifiable contract
chapters.source_title: Managing Cloud Limits

pages.title: 12 · The cloud has limits and lead times

blocks.caption: Original official publication, accessed 23 October 2026.

blocks.text: A Nubank engineering publication describes multiple accounts, sharding, and monitoring of utilization, quotas, and costs. The case presents capacity as a shared responsibility between platform and domains. The article's scale figures are historical; this chapter does not depend on treating them as a current inventory. The question is how to turn consumption signals into decisions before a journey hits a limit.

A quota is more than a configuration entry. It has a scope, unit, source, increase lead time, and relationship to dependencies. Limits may apply by region, account, resource, or service. An application can have CPU available yet be unable to create the connections, addresses, or components it needs. Planning only the most visible dimension creates a false sense of headroom. The capacity model must represent the bottleneck relevant to the journey.

The proposal combines an inventory of limits, explicit forecasting, and reservations before admitting planned changes. The lab tests multidimensional reservations and local concurrency without provisioning resources. It simulates neither AWS nor Kubernetes. Its role is to demonstrate that two teams cannot simultaneously consume the same promised headroom. Production design would require fresh sources, reconciliation of reservations against actual resources, and handling the delay between requesting capacity and having it available.

pages.chapter_title: Cloud capacity as a product commitment

pages.title: Observed, reserved, and available are different quantities

blocks.text: Observed consumption describes what a source measured. A reservation describes accepted intent not yet reflected in that measurement. Safety margin represents capacity we do not want to commit during normal operation. Safe availability is the limit minus those three components, respecting each resource's unit. Mixing reservations and observed consumption can count the same demand twice or, worse, not count it at all.

In the lab, baselines are constant and reservations are maintained under a lock. There is no provisioning, so no automatic transition from reservation to actual consumption exists. This limitation avoids hiding the hardest problem: reconciling the request identifier, created resource, and subsequent measurement. A real implementation would need states such as requested, reserved, provisioning, observed, and closed, with defined timeouts and recovery for each.

Capacity is multidimensional. Demand is accepted only when every required dimension fits; reserving CPU and failing on a network address would leave a useless fragment without atomicity. The model rejects the whole request, allowing the team to revise its size or schedule. Priority policy must also be explicit. A critical expansion may justify a different decision, but the exception needs an owner and evidence, not an informal path that ignores the margin without a record.

pages.chapter_title: Cloud capacity as a product commitment

pages.title: From quota to launch commitment
pages.kicker: PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · NOT AN INTERNAL DESIGN

blocks.title: From quota to launch commitment
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture. Boxes represent responsibilities; arrows make contracts explicit.

blocks.text: The collector normalizes units and records source freshness. A quota without recent data should not appear unlimited. The inventory separates scopes to avoid comparing consumption in one region with a limit in another. Forecasting produces scenarios, not certainties: linear growth can help anticipation, but does not automatically describe campaigns or concentrated events.

Admission links capacity to the launch commitment. It reserves every relevant dimension and tracks provisioning outcomes. Asynchronous feedback avoids holding a transaction open while a provider creates resources. Reconciliation must recognize completed operations whose responses were lost, as well as abandoned reservations. The journey supplies priority and schedule; the platform supplies headroom and required time. This contract enables evidence-based discussion of delay, reduced scope, or expansion without turning a technical estimate into a promise of unlimited availability.

pages.chapter_title: Cloud capacity as a product commitment

pages.title: Multidimensional reservations without local overbooking

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_12.py. Synthetic in-memory reservation; provisions neither AWS nor Kubernetes.

blocks.text: The executed code calculates and commits availability under the same lock. Two threads cannot promise the same headroom. Token history remains after release: replay recognizes the closed operation without recreating the reservation; different content raises a conflict. New intent requires a new token. Independent copies protect records from changes to the supplied dictionary.

The lock protects one process, and history is volatile with no retention policy. Distributed coordination would require persistence, atomic comparison, and expiry tied to the replay window. The lab specifies behavior; local memory neither governs real resources nor provides idempotency after restart.

pages.chapter_title: Cloud capacity as a product commitment

pages.title: Prometheus: alert on headroom and stale data

blocks.code:
groups:
  - name: portfolio-capacity
    rules:
      - alert: SafeCapacityExhausted
        expr: portfolio_safe_headroom < 0
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          owner: platform-demo
        annotations:
          summary: "Margem segura negativa"
          description: "Revisar reservas e demanda planejada."
      - alert: CapacitySourceStale
        expr: time() - portfolio_capacity_collected_at > 900
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          owner: platform-demo
        annotations:
          summary: "Fonte de capacidade desatualizada"
          description: "Confirmar coleta antes de admitir expansão."

# Métricas, limiares e responsável são exemplos propostos.
# Validar regras com dados e ferramentas do ambiente real.
blocks.caption: Reference YAML, not executed. Metrics and names are proposed, not internal Nubank telemetry.

blocks.text: The reference rules distinguish insufficient headroom from insufficient information. If collection stops, a stable dashboard can look healthy while consumption keeps growing. Source age must inform operational decisions. The example thresholds are synthetic and require calibration against collection frequency and available reaction time.

Prometheus can evaluate these conditions, but an alert neither reserves capacity nor requests a quota increase. The owner needs a verifiable procedure and access to sources. Labels should use controlled dimensions such as account and quota type, avoiding per-request identifiers that would multiply time series without proportional benefit.
