chapters.title: Precog: reaching the right specialist
chapters.subtitle: AI · Customer support
chapters.source_title: Presenting Precog, Nubank’s Real Time Event AI

pages.title: Routing is a hypothesis about a need

blocks.caption: Original official publication, accessed 23 October 2026.

blocks.text: In June 2023, Nubank introduced Precog, which uses event representations to support intent models. The article reports an increase of more than 50% in the volume of calls correctly routed to specialists without customer input, compared with the previous model. That result belongs to the implementation and period described in the publication. It does not mean a gain of fifty percentage points, does not automatically measure resolution, and is not a target this laboratory can promise to reproduce.

The study opportunity lies in sustaining that quality as products, events, and reasons for contact change. A prediction can be technically confident and wrong about what the person needs now. It can also identify the product correctly and route the person to an unavailable queue. I would assess routing as an operational decision that can be corrected, rather than a classification that ends the effort to understand the customer. Support must be able to challenge the suggestion and preserve useful context.

This chapter's laboratory uses synthetic event weights, without embeddings or training. It tests time windows, deduplication, minimum support, abstention, and declared priority. The intention is to make those boundaries verifiable before discussing better models. A weight distribution is not a calibrated probability. The code demonstrates policy, not predictive quality, and grants no authority to block an account, transfer funds, or make any financial decision on someone's behalf.

sources.title: Presenting Precog, Nubank’s Real Time Event AI

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Intent, urgency, and availability are different things

blocks.text: The domain needs to distinguish the probable reason for contact, declared urgency, and support capacity. Someone who has just attempted a payment may be calling for another reason. A risk signal may require specialist triage even when the likely product is a card. And a queue with capable specialists may be unavailable at that time. Combining everything into a single score makes the result harder to explain and would hide decisions governed by different policies.

I would model the recommendation as a record containing the suggested intent, evidence used, policy version, reason for abstention, and operational destination. The person and the support agent need a simple way to correct the reason. That correction should not automatically be treated as a perfect label: the customer may raise several topics, the agent may choose a convenient category, and another team may resolve the issue. Taxonomy quality requires joint work with Operations.

In the laboratory, declared urgency leads to a dedicated human queue, independently of the ranking. Insufficient events or an intent without an available queue lead to general triage. These are educational choices, not Nubank policies. A real implementation would need to validate capacity, schedules, languages, and accessibility needs. The important contract separates recognizing a pattern from deciding how to provide help; neither decision should remove the opportunity to explain the problem.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: A recommendation with a human path

blocks.title: A recommendation with a human path

nodes.label: Event ingestion
nodes.detail: Kafka as a proposed option; versioned contract

blocks.caption: Original reference architecture with proposed queue names and boundaries. It does not reproduce internal systems.

blocks.text: The public article describes event consumption and Clojure/Python services, but Kafka's use in this design is a reference choice, not a claim about Precog. The boundary between ranking and policy prevents queue availability from being confused with model confidence. The chosen destination must carry a reason Operations can understand and allow correction without restarting the story. Outcomes return asynchronously for evaluation after considering how the contact ended. A corrected label does not rewrite the original decision: it records what was known and what was learned. The laboratory implements a window, weighted ranking, and in-memory policy. It includes no embeddings, telephony, or real queue. In production, I would prefer to integrate existing capabilities and measure the additional cost of a recommendation before introducing a new service into the support path.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Abstaining is also a valid decision

blocks.caption: Executed excerpt from case_16.py. Ranking uses invented weights; it does not implement Precog. Types, imports, and validators are in the complete file.

blocks.text: The function applies urgency before ranking, requires minimum support, and avoids a nonexistent queue. The share field represents the winning intent's share of weight, not its probability of being correct. The 0.75 threshold is synthetic. An ML implementation would need confidence calibration by intent and monitoring of abstention quality, rather than copying these numbers. Human fallback is a functional path, not a hidden error. The rule also does not manage capacity: available is an already resolved input. If it is stale, the destination must reject the request with a defined recovery path. Invalid types and domains raise ValueError before any favorable result.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Pure policy in Clojure, effects at another boundary

blocks.code:
(ns independent.support-policy)

(defn choose-route
  [{:keys [urgent? available candidates min-support]}]
  (let [ordered (sort-by (juxt (comp - :weight) :intent)
                         candidates)
        total (reduce + (map :weight ordered))
        best (first ordered)
        share (if (pos? total)
                (/ (:weight best 0) total)
                0)]
    (cond
      urgent?
      {:queue :human-urgent :reason :declared-urgency}

      (< total min-support)
      {:queue :human-general :reason :insufficient}

      (or (< share 3/4)
          (not (contains? available (:intent best))))
      {:queue :human-general :reason :abstention}

      :else
      {:queue (:intent best)
       :reason :ranked
       :share share})))

;; O adaptador persiste e encaminha fora desta função.
;; Contrato proposto: candidate weights >= 0.
;; Empates recebem ordem determinística, não mais confiança.
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure, not executed; namespaces, queues, and policy are external proposals.

blocks.text: The proposed function receives immutable data and returns a recommendation without calling telephony, recording effects, or updating shared state. This makes policy easier to test separately from integration. Clojure is part of Nubank's published technical context; this fragment is independent and was not executed. Weight validation and a consistent availability read belong to the adapter. Using an atom in a prototype does not provide persistence or a transaction with external systems. Functions passed to mechanisms that may repeat evaluation must remain free of effects. Routing needs its own identity and reconciliation outside the calculation.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Event time and knowledge time

blocks.text: An event may occur before a contact and arrive afterward. Reconstructing the decision with every event we know today would create an artificially favorable evaluation. I would record separately when the fact occurred and when it became available to the router. A replay must respect both. This boundary is particularly important on mobile networks, where signals may remain on the device and be transmitted in a batch after the person reconnects.

The local window discards future events, events outside the period, and old receipts, while rejecting conflicting duplicates. The limits of 180 and 30 units are synthetic parameters, not recommended minutes for Nubank. The experiment must declare its unit and clock. An inaccurate client clock may require additional validation or another reference; comparing numbers as if every machine shared exactly the same time is not enough.

A stable event key helps deduplicate delivery attempts but does not identify two different interactions of the same type. I would avoid discarding events simply because their attributes look similar. In the proposed Kafka integration, committing an offset does not confirm routing in the support system. Those effects belong to different boundaries. The design would need a durable decision record and reconciliation to determine whether an unknown routing attempt can be repeated without transferring the customer again.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: The costliest error may be a plausible queue

blocks.text: A model may route most contacts correctly while failing on the most urgent topics. An aggregate average would hide that pattern. I would stratify evaluation by intent, urgency, new product, and cases without history, always showing sample size and uncertainty. I would also observe when a specialist corrects the destination, how much time that takes, and whether the person has to repeat sensitive information. Quality does not end with selecting the first queue correctly.

A change in event naming can gradually reduce context without taking the service down. Another failure occurs when the predicted intent no longer has an available team. The contract must provide a general path and preserve the suggested reason as a hypothesis. Keeping a person in a transfer loop because each component considers its own decision correct is unacceptable. The system must recognize repeated routing and escalate to a human resolution path with clear responsibility.

I would also test manipulated or repeated events without turning this chapter into instructions about internal controls. The principle is straightforward: behavioral telemetry is limited evidence, never an access credential. Visiting particular screens does not grant financial authorization. Changes to destination, priority, or context must respect support and privacy policies. The laboratory demonstrates abstention and deduplication; abuse testing, telephony, and real operations remain outside its scope.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Fifteen policy checks, no accuracy promise

blocks.text: The fifteen tests in case_16.py passed locally. They check a dominant intent, ambiguity, missing evidence, urgency, an unavailable queue, duplication, conflict, future events, an old occurrence received now, an old receipt, a negative weight, and insufficient support. Each test makes a claim about policy and windows, not about understanding human intent. The result does not validate embeddings, measure support, or prove the chosen threshold appropriate for any product. Additional regressions reject nonfinite, fractional, and boolean weights, as well as invalid policy and clocks.

In the demonstration, weights of eight for card and one for Pix route to card with a share of approximately 0.889. Equal weights produce abstention and general triage. These examples show why a decision can be reproduced, but they also expose the method's limits. Invented weights can produce a convincing recommendation that is completely wrong about a person. The correct interpretation is that the mechanism respected the synthetic contract, not that it achieved a particular level of predictive quality.

A real evaluation would require reviewed labels, a separate temporal dataset, treatment of multiple intents, and analysis of repeat contacts. I would involve support specialists in discussing errors rather than relying solely on a confusion matrix. We would need to measure resolution and repeat contact, because apparently fast routing may simply postpone the work. The decision to proceed would depend on those outcomes and on support's capacity to absorb fallback paths.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Metrics that follow through to resolution

blocks.text: The first metric would be correct routing under an agreed, reviewable definition. It must specify whether the destination was equipped to resolve the issue, whether a transfer occurred, and whether multiple topics make classification ambiguous. I would then track time to useful assistance, repeat contact, and first-contact resolution without claiming causality merely because these measures move together. Changes in team, staffing, or policy may affect the outcome independently of the model.

Abstention deserves its own dashboard. A low rate is not necessarily better: it may indicate overconfidence. A high rate may be a responsible choice for new cases, but it can also reveal missing events. I would show evidence coverage, recency, and fallback reasons by intent while preserving sufficiently aggregated groups. The dashboard should distinguish collection, model, policy, and operational-availability problems. Without that separation, every investigation ends up in the same data queue.

Each alert would need to point to an action. Loss of recency may trigger a pipeline investigation; increased transfers for an intent may suspend its automation; an unavailable queue requires an Operations decision. The model owner cannot resolve the third situation alone. I would record model and policy versions with every decision to compare changes in context. Logs should not contain free-form transcripts or identifiers unnecessary to answer the operational question that justified collecting them.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Shadow evaluation with outcomes, then limited exposure

blocks.text: The first evaluation could run recommendations without changing routing. For each eligible contact, we would compare the suggestion with the observed destination and outcome, recognizing that the existing flow can also be wrong. The review design must include easy and difficult contacts, not just cases with a clear conclusion. A sample excluding abandonments, repeat contacts, or unknown categories can produce an optimistic evaluation precisely where the mechanism most needs oversight.

A controlled pilot could then automate only intents with sufficient evidence, preserving a human path and immediate correction. The population, limits, and pause conditions would be defined before exposure. I would not start with urgent topics or scenarios where an incorrect transfer could delay necessary protection. Those paths need specific policies developed with their owners, rather than an exception improvised after the first significant incident.

As an EM, I would align support capacity, training, and availability to review errors during the first weeks. As a Staff engineer, I would ensure decision replay, contract versions, and event compatibility. The pilot should lead to a choice: expand the intent, change the threshold, improve context, or return to triage. I would not treat increasing coverage as an isolated objective. Benefit depends on better routing and resolution with less effort, while preserving a person's right to explain a need the prediction does not capture.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Privacy and separation of authority

blocks.text: Support context can reveal habits and financial difficulties. I would apply minimization from the definition of signals onward, avoiding free-form descriptions or transaction content in a pipeline that only needs to recognize interaction categories. Pseudonymizing identifiers reduces exposure but does not automatically anonymize the dataset. Access, retention, and purpose must remain explicit, with input from privacy and security owners. Assessing benefit does not remove these design obligations.

A queue recommendation must not change limits, release operations, or serve as proof of identity. That separation appears in the code and must also exist in service permissions. A component classifying intent may access limited signals, while performing a financial action requires a different contract and authority. Combining the two for convenience would create a path in which behavioral inference acquires power it should never possess.

Performance belongs at this boundary too. If ranking exceeds its time budget, support must continue through a known route. The general queue cannot depend on the same resource that just failed. I would estimate inference cost per eligible contact and monitor context storage without choosing retention solely to make experimentation easier. A sophisticated model that delays assistance or expands collection without proven benefit may be inferior to a simple, well-operated policy.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: ADR: automate with explicit abstention

blocks.text: The proposed decision separates intent calculation, routing policy, and operational execution, treating abstention as a normal outcome. A fixed rule based on the last screen is simple, but it may confuse recent navigation with the current need. A more expressive model may increase coverage, but it requires evaluation, maintenance, and interpretation of errors. The laboratory chooses a small rule to make boundaries examinable; it does not recommend replacing Precog or claim superiority over the published work.

The advantage of separation is being able to change a queue policy without retraining the model and evaluate a new model without changing the support integration. The cost is maintaining contracts and versions between components and preventing inconsistencies when a queue changes name or becomes unavailable. The persisted decision should record the destination catalog in effect. If this complexity does not solve an observed problem, the mechanism can remain within an existing service rather than becoming three new services.

I would revisit the ADR if human corrections suggested an unsuitable taxonomy, useful coverage were small, or maintaining context cost more than the gain. I would also consider a short question to the customer a legitimate alternative: sometimes asking is better than inferring. The choice should compare total effort and resolution quality, not just how many contacts avoid an initial interaction. The person seeking help remains the primary source about their own need.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

pages.title: Useful capacity and responsibility for the queue

blocks.text: The first deliverable would be one intent with an event contract, an abstention policy, label review, and outcome tracking. Operations would participate from problem definition onward, because correct routing depends on how support works. As an EM, I would reserve time for joint error review and training, avoiding placing the entire cost of a technical experiment on support agents. I would also define who can suspend automation for an intent.

Economic value would be estimated from avoided transfers, work minutes that can actually be recovered, and the mechanism's incremental cost. A realization factor is essential: saving seconds on average does not automatically reduce expenses. Repeat contacts, longer handling time in another queue, and review work must be included in the comparison. Customer time saved would be reported separately as an experience outcome. I would not add transfer and contact reductions when they describe the same avoided effort.

My Staff question would be: can we reproduce what the router knew when it decided, including available queues and the policy version? My EM question would be: when the prediction is wrong, is a person or team responsible and able to resolve the issue without restarting the journey? The answer connects architecture and leadership. The goal is useful help with less repetition while preserving room to correct a hypothesis that seemed plausible.

pages.chapter_title: Precog: reaching the right specialist

lab.scope: Synthetic routing using weights and windows; 15 tests. No embeddings, training, Kafka, or telephony executed.

chapters.title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey
chapters.subtitle: Security · Machine Learning
chapters.source_title: Practices to scale Machine Learning operations

pages.title: Protection within the time the experience allows

blocks.caption: Original official publication, accessed 23 October 2026.

blocks.text: In April 2025, Nubank published practices for operating real-time models, including a Model Server with Clojure and Python, feature retrieval, optimization, and shadow mode. The article provides technical context but does not disclose decision policies, risk thresholds, or losses by product. This study does not identify a vulnerability or attempt to infer those controls. It starts with an engineering question: how do we preserve a responsible decision when context and time are limited?

In a financial journey, waiting indefinitely is also a choice with consequences. Allowing everything when a dependency fails is another choice, often an inappropriate one. Between those extremes are decisions based on context, recovery, and review. I would discuss with Risk which evidence is indispensable, what can be missing, and how the person continues when an operation cannot be authorized immediately. That conversation cannot be delegated to a score without explaining its purpose and limits.

The laboratory uses a logistic function with invented, fixed parameters. There is no training, calibration, or Nubank dataset. The objective is to demonstrate the separation of calculation, policy, and error cost, including false positives. Sixteen tests verify this small contract. They do not demonstrate fraud-detection capability, loss reduction, or regulatory suitability. The examples provide a basis for discussing how I would turn an ambiguous decision into a safe experiment with domain specialists.

sources.title: Practices to scale Machine Learning operations

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: The score is not the decision

blocks.text: A number between zero and one may look like a probability, but that appearance does not guarantee calibration. Before using it, we need to know what it attempts to predict, over which horizon, with which data, and under what conditions. The local model merely transforms synthetic signals into a value that can be ranked. Calling it a probability of fraud would conceal a property that has never been measured. This distinction is central to preventing mathematical presentation from granting policy unwarranted authority.

The laboratory policy chooses allow, review, or block, with specific outcomes for missing and stale data. Thresholds are decision parameters, not natural characteristics of the model. A threshold change can alter review volume, friction, and losses while the model remains identical. I would version these elements separately so an incident could be attributed to the right change. I would also record the limits of each action: review does not mean condemnation, and blocking an attempt does not necessarily block the account.

Review must be a real capability. Without a team, deadline, or recovery path, an intermediate state becomes an invisible queue. In the proposal, each outcome would have an appropriate message, next step, and observability without revealing sensitive mechanisms. The technical contract must support an understandable experience. Model quality matters, but customer trust also depends on how the system handles uncertainty and allows an incorrect decision to be corrected.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Evidence, policy, and effects at separate boundaries

blocks.title: Evidence, policy, and effects at separate boundaries

nodes.label: Model
nodes.detail: Score and version; bounded time budget

blocks.caption: Independent architecture. It does not describe Nubank’s internal thresholds, policies, or components.

blocks.text: A risk decision does not replace authentication, authorization, or financial consistency. The component producing the effect must validate appropriate authority at the operation boundary even when policy recommends allowing it. Features arrive with version and temporal information so absence is not confused with a normal value. The review path needs its own capacity and deadlines; it is not a repository for cases the model could not classify. Evaluation receives outcomes after labels mature, avoiding calling a transaction legitimate simply because no dispute has yet appeared. The laboratory implements only a score, policy, and synthetic error accounting. It performs no authorization, production detection, or support. Python and Clojure are technologies cited in the public source; the organization shown here is an original proposal that would need comparison with existing boundaries before any integration.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: An educational model and an explicit policy

blocks.caption: Executed excerpt from case_17.py. Fixed, untrained toy logistic model. Types, imports, and validators are in the complete file.

blocks.text: The coefficients were chosen to produce different test paths; they were not learned and do not represent real risk. The calculated value is named probability_like to emphasize that limit. Stale or missing data leads to synthetic review, while negative inputs are rejected. The 0.30 and 0.85 thresholds must not be transferred into operations. A real implementation requires evaluation of discrimination, calibration, stability, and error cost, plus a formal fallback decision. The code preserves the separation between producing a score and selecting an action. It contains no internal controls, actual fraud rules, or financial integration. Invalid types and domains raise ValueError before any favorable result.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Separate loss, false positives, and review

blocks.caption: Function and scenario executed in case_17.py; synthetic costs, not a projection for Nubank. Types, imports, and validators are in the complete file.

blocks.text: Money remains in integer cents, and the components stay identifiable. In the example, allowed fraud costs 10,000 cents, an incorrect block costs 500, and a review costs 100, totaling 10,600. These are arbitrary simulation costs. The function does not model recovery, residual losses after review, reputation, or long-term effects. In particular, review does not guarantee fraud prevention; its full cost depends on the outcome. This decomposition avoids hiding false positives behind an aggregate accuracy metric, but it becomes useful for investment only when each component has its own definition and evidence.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: A feature snapshot needs meaning

blocks.text: Two features named velocity may measure different things: attempts, confirmed operations, or observed devices. Even when both are integers, their semantics can differ. I would require a shared definition specifying the window, unit, source, and treatment of absence. The model should not receive a zero produced by a timeout as if it meant no activity. This confusion changes the interpretation of the customer without necessarily producing a visible technical service error.

Freshness is also domain-specific. Registration information may tolerate a different age from a signal associated with the current attempt. The laboratory's single age_seconds field is only a simplification for testing the stale-data branch. In production, I would assess freshness per feature and decision. Essential data needs an unavailability policy; optional data needs evidence that the model can operate without it under the evaluated conditions.

The inference snapshot should be traceable within privacy constraints, without requiring indiscriminate retention of sensitive data. Versioned definitions and metadata may suffice for some investigations; others require governed samples. The choice depends on purpose and the confirmation period. The team must be able to explain which information supported a decision and which was missing, without retrospectively inventing context that arrived only after the operation.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: A partial failure must not become blanket permission

blocks.text: A slow dependency can extend journey time and consume resources needed by other requests. Setting a timeout limits that harm but does not decide what happens next. I would separate the technical budget from risk policy: first, how long can we wait; then, what decision is acceptable without that context? The second answer belongs to the domain and may vary by operation, remaining evidence, and exposure. A generic permissive fallback is not an automatic engineering conclusion.

Reviewing everything also carries risk. A broad incident can exceed human-queue capacity, delaying recovery for legitimate customers. The plan must recognize saturation and define previously agreed actions, clear messaging, and appropriate priority. Review must not become a word that hides unavailability. Monitoring should show arrivals, departures, wait time, and case age, alongside the rate of degraded decisions creating the additional demand.

I would test missing, delayed, inconsistent, and subsequently recovered data without assuming all require the same response. I would also rehearse a new feature-producer version interacting with an old model. The laboratory covers only a small portion of these scenarios using local structures. It does not simulate queue capacity or distributed concurrency. Those limits matter: passing policy tests does not demonstrate that the system will remain safe during an operational failure at scale.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Sixteen tests and a result that fits in a table

blocks.text: The laboratory successfully ran sixteen tests. They check low, high, and intermediate scores; missing, stale, and future data; negative inputs; invalid threshold ordering; velocity monotonicity; cost decomposition; correct actions with no modeled cost; and an unknown action. Monotonicity is a property of the chosen coefficients, not evidence that velocity must always increase real-world risk. The suite makes the demonstration consistent and reproducible. The review added rejection of nonfinite numbers, fractional cents, ambiguous flags, and unknown review actions.

The economic output adds 10,000 cents of allowed fraud, 500 of false-positive cost, and 100 of review cost. The 10,600-cent total does not represent a company's savings or losses. It is a fixture result, useful for checking that the implementation adds different categories without losing the unit. The correct-action scenario returns zero because the cost model excludes fixed expenses, infrastructure, and residual friction. This must remain explicit so the result does not look like perfect efficiency.

Subsequent validation would require authorized data, temporal separation of training and evaluation, label maturation, and baseline comparison. I would assess segments and degraded scenarios as well as the average. Review cost would depend on actual operations and what happens after triage. Only then could we discuss thresholds. The local artifact demonstrates contract discipline; the quality of a fraud-prevention policy requires different evidence and participation from the responsible specialists.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Measure protection and friction on the same dashboard

blocks.text: I would avoid choosing a single metric to declare success. Confirmed fraud, legitimate transactions blocked, review, and latency need to appear together with their denominators and maturation periods. A policy blocking everything may appear excellent at prevention while making the product unusable. A policy allowing everything may look excellent at immediate completion and accumulate losses later. The decision requires understanding the trade-off among these outcomes rather than celebrating one in isolation.

Label quality directly affects that interpretation. A transaction without a dispute may still be undiscovered fraud; a dispute may be reversed. I would record the window used and revise time series when updates occur while preserving earlier versions. I would also examine selection bias: blocked decisions may never reveal what would have happened if allowed. Comparing groups without considering that difference would produce weak causal conclusions and could lead to unsuitable thresholds.

Operationally, I would monitor time per dependency, missing features, and the proportion of degraded decisions. Correlation between those signals and customer outcomes guides investigation but does not establish cause on its own. Alerts should reach owners able to act on the model, data, or policy. An increase in false positives requires different context from an infrastructure failure. I would keep this responsibility map alongside the dashboard so observability helps resolve the identified problem.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Shadow mode can teach without authorizing money

blocks.text: A candidate model can produce scores alongside the current flow without changing the real decision. This stage enables output comparison and detection of feature incompatibilities, but it does not eliminate every risk: additional collection consumes resources, processing can delay dependencies, and retention requires governance. I would define an execution budget and isolation so the experiment does not harm the operation it seeks to improve. Shadow mode is an evaluation method, not an exemption from operational responsibility.

Differences between the candidate and baseline would be analyzed by case type and outcome, with Risk and Operations involved. I would not assume disagreement means improvement. We might discover that a new model identifies useful patterns but performs worse for an underrepresented population, or that its gain comes from information unavailable at the actual decision time. Proceeding would require reproducing temporal conditions and validating policy cost, not merely comparing offline performance curves.

Limited exposure would require containment criteria, authority to pause, and a support plan for affected customers. I would also assess model and policy rollback separately. Restoring a version does not undo blocks or delays that have already happened; those effects may need specific recovery. As an EM, I would ensure capacity for that work. As a Staff engineer, I would maintain sufficient contracts and traceability to know what was decided, using which data and version.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Less data, clearer boundaries

blocks.text: Access to a feature should not be granted merely because it might improve a model. Purpose, availability, and protection need justification, favoring representations that reduce exposure while preserving usefulness. Decision logs must not become an unrestricted copy of the customer's financial context. I would discuss with Security and Privacy what information is needed for investigation, for how long, and under which access controls. The design must support evaluation without distributing sensitive data across every team involved.

I would also separate permissions to read context, publish a model, change policy, and execute financial actions. A failure in one component should not give the same process all these capabilities. The laboratory has no identity, network, or credentials, so it does not demonstrate such isolation. In a real integration, I would use existing tools and standards while explicitly assessing who can change a threshold and how that change is reviewed, recorded, and reversed when necessary.

Technology choices must respect the environment. Python suits the educational core and appears in Nubank's public architecture, while Clojure appears in the described integration. This does not mean every proposal should create a new model server. Improving a feature contract, compatibility test, or metric on the current platform may be more useful. The investment should address an observed gap, with operational cost proportional to the expected benefit and the team's ability to sustain it.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: ADR: version policy separately from the score

blocks.text: The proposed decision keeps the model as a signal producer and policy responsible for the action, with independent versions. Embedding thresholds and fallback within the model artifact simplifies deployment but mixes different kinds of change. Distributing rules across consumers offers flexibility and may create divergences that are difficult to trace. I would start with an explicit contract where the decision already occurs, avoiding a new platform without a demonstrated need.

The benefit is explaining whether an outcome changed because of the signal, context, or policy. The cost is maintaining compatibility and preventing unevaluated combinations. A new model should not be promoted with just any old policy merely because its output format is identical. The version record must include conditions of use and expected data. Operations also needs to know which combinations are supported during migration and which forms the rollback path.

I would revisit the decision if separation added latency without useful benefit, or if the domain required a joint deployment to preserve consistency. Logical separation does not require a remote call between services. The same process can maintain distinct modules and contracts. The question is not how many boxes appear in the diagram, but whether a team can evaluate, change, and operate the decision without losing its history, limits, or responsibility for its effects.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

pages.title: Economic outcomes with human responsibility

blocks.text: The first increment could be a critical-feature contract and a policy evaluation in shadow mode with discrepancy review. As an EM, I would align Engineering, Data Science, Risk, and Support around objectives covering protection and experience. I would also reserve capacity for false-positive analysis and recovery so the improvement backlog does not overlook affected customers. Leadership must turn this discussion into clear priorities, owners, and criteria for stopping the experiment.

The economic model would compare fraud losses under equivalent conditions, the cost of blocked legitimate transactions, review cost, and incremental infrastructure. I would not substitute accuracy for value. Friction costs need definition: additional support, operational time, and demonstrated lost usage are different measures. Benefits sharing the same event must not be counted twice. Without evidence, I would present a range of assumptions and sensitivity analysis rather than calling the number realized savings.

My Staff question would be: what information can be missing without invalidating the decision, and who approved that boundary? My EM question would be: do we have the capacity to correct the decision when a legitimate person cannot proceed? These questions connect the technical contract to teamwork. The goal is not an impressive classifier in isolation. It is a protection system that responds within the journey's time constraints and remains accountable for the errors it inevitably needs to recognize and address.

pages.chapter_title: Fraud prevention that responds within the journey

chapters.title: The same feature in training and at decision time
chapters.subtitle: Data · ML quality
chapters.source_title: Dealing with Train-serve Skew in Real-time ML Models: A Short Guide

pages.title: The same name, different decisions

blocks.caption: Original official publication, accessed 23 October 2026.

blocks.text: Nubank's public guide to train-serve skew, published in June 2023, discusses differences between data used for training and inference. Examples include different time windows, absence represented as zero, and incompatible sources. These are educational examples of a class of problem, not evidence of specific incidents or customer losses. This chapter uses that context to explore a feature contract that can be compared without reconstructing the past using future information.

A feature may have the correct name, type, and numeric range while still representing something else. Training may count confirmed purchases over sixty days, while the service counts attempts over thirty. Both produce plausible integers. No exception needs to be raised for the model to start receiving information outside the meaning on which it was built. The problem requires semantic observation, not just format validation or endpoint availability.

The laboratory implements a windowed sum with two clocks: occurrence and knowledge. It also generates a contract identity and compares values, absence, and version. Everything uses invented events and integer cents. Fifteen tests verify temporal boundaries, duplication, late information, and contract incompatibility. The objective is not to build a feature store, but to demonstrate the minimum needed for a precise question: can we reproduce the information available when the decision actually happened?

sources.title: Dealing with Train-serve Skew in Real-time ML Models: A Short Guide

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: The contract contains more than the type

blocks.text: I would define a feature by name, unit, entity, window, temporal boundaries, the state of included events, source, and missingness rule. I would also record which subsequent corrections change the value and how they affect historical replays. Without these choices, two teams can correctly implement different specifications and discover the divergence only when model behavior changes. A textual description helps, but it needs executable examples that expose boundary cases.

In the laboratory, the window is open on the left and closed on the right: an event exactly at the start is excluded; an event at decision time can be included if it was already known. The unit is cents, and an unavailable source produces None. An available source with no events produces zero. This difference is small in code and important to the decision: zero describes an empty observation, while None describes missing observation. The model may need to treat these states differently.

Contract identity derives from a canonical representation of its parameters. It helps detect incompatible combinations but does not prove that the implementation follows the declared meaning. A service can publish the correct hash while calculating the wrong window. I would therefore combine contract verification with example comparison and replays. Documentation defines what should happen; tests and observations show whether producers and consumers are actually doing the same thing.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Reproduce the decision without knowing the future

blocks.title: Reproduce the decision without knowing the future
blocks.caption: Original design. Proposed contracts and names; it does not represent an internal feature store.

blocks.text: The comparator should compare only values representing the same entity, instant, and definition. Replay receives a knowledge cutoff to prevent later-arriving events from making the past artificially complete. The contract governs online and offline paths but does not replace implementation validation. The divergence record retains enough references to investigate, with retention and access proportionate to the data. A mismatch does not automatically imply an online error: it may reflect a historical correction, a legitimate availability difference, or a defect in the replay itself. The laboratory represents these concepts in memory and does not run a distributed pipeline. In production, I would look for existing capture points to reduce cost and avoid another complete event copy. Investigation needs to reach the owners of feature meaning, not just the team operating storage or the model.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Information the system did not yet have

blocks.caption: Executed excerpt from case_18.py; synthetic events and clocks. Types, imports, and validators are in the complete file.

blocks.text: The occurred field represents when the event happened; known indicates when it entered the available set. Replay excludes data not known at the chosen cutoff, even if it occurred before the decision. The window boundary is explicit too. This structure does not resolve corrections, deletions, or multiple versions of an event: conflicting duplicates raise an error so the case is not silently aggregated. A real integration would need its own policy for those states. The demonstration uses integers as a synthetic clock; production timestamps require a unit, time zone, precision, and validation agreed among the components involved.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Compare meaning before comparing numbers

blocks.caption: Functions and examples executed in case_18.py. The hash identifies parameters; it does not certify implementation. Types, imports, and validators are in the complete file.

blocks.text: Equal values can hide different contracts. The comparison therefore checks definition identity first, then missingness, and finally the numeric difference. The shortened digest is convenient for the demonstration and must not be treated as a security signature. In production, the version needs a link to a governed registry and the published implementation. Tolerance also belongs to the domain: an exact monetary sum may require equality, while another feature permits bounded numeric error. A large tolerance does not fix incompatible semantics; it merely turns a divergence into something monitoring stops displaying. Nonfinite values and invalid tolerance raise ValueError, preventing a false match.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Absence, zero, and delay are not synonyms

blocks.text: An available source may return no occurrences because the customer did not perform the activity. Under the local contract, that produces zero. An unavailable source provides no such information and produces absence. A late event may make the current value differ from what becomes known later without indicating a defect in the original implementation. Converting all these states to zero gives the model a simplification that erases precisely the context needed to interpret the decision.

I would carry this distinction into the schema and evaluation. An optional field should not exist merely to avoid serialization failure; its meaning must be documented and compatible with training. I would also avoid using a special string as a numeric value without governance. The consumer must know whether the feature is missing because of no history, technical unavailability, or an eligibility condition. In some domains, these causes may require different treatment, but that decision needs validation with specialists.

The laboratory uses only an available or unavailable source without classifying every possible cause. This keeps the example inspectable. For a real pilot, I would start with a critical feature and investigate which states actually occur rather than inventing a complete taxonomy in advance. Contract evolution would include old and new examples so richer expression does not silently break consumers still using earlier versions.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Late events can mislead an otherwise sound evaluation

blocks.text: Consider a purchase that occurred before the decision but reached the platform afterward. A dataset reconstructed weeks later may include it as though it had always been available. The model evaluated offline appears to use complete context, while the online service never had that opportunity. This difference does not require an algorithmic bug. The problem is the question asked of history: are we reconstructing the world as it was, or the world as it later became known?

Another situation involves corrections and reprocessing. A value may be adjusted later, a duplicate removed, or an event reclassified. Replay must define whether the intended reference is the original or corrected view, preserving both when the purpose requires it. Rewriting every old report with current data destroys the ability to explain past decisions. Yet ignoring corrections forever prevents learning. The solution depends on versioning references and the purpose of comparison.

I would also test day and time-zone boundaries, window changes, and out-of-order events. The laboratory uses integer time to isolate the reasoning, so it does not demonstrate civil-time handling. That layer would require additional tests with time-zone-aware timestamps and agreed rules. The criterion is not having many calendar tests, but checking instants when two plausible implementations might include different event sets and produce incompatible decisions.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Fifteen tests to avoid a perfect past

blocks.text: The fifteen local tests passed. They cover equivalent values, future occurrence, late knowledge, an open left boundary, duplication, conflict, absence differing from zero, absence on both sides, an incompatible contract, tolerance, an unavailable source, and an invalid window. The suite checks the example's declared semantics. It does not demonstrate model quality, absence of skew in a real environment, or correctness of any Nubank implementation. These results belong only to the independent package accompanying the chapter. Additional regressions reject NaN, infinity, invalid tolerance, and events outside the integer time-and-cents contract.

In the demonstration, a decision at 100 knows about an event worth 200 cents. Another event occurred at 95 but became known only at 110. With a knowledge cutoff of 100, the sum is 200; with a cutoff of 120, the historical sum becomes 1,100. Both results can be correct for different questions. The mistake would be using the second as proof that the service should have calculated that value at the first instant without acknowledging the unavailable information.

The next step would compare online capture and replay over an authorized set, with sampling that includes missingness and version changes. I would examine divergences manually before choosing an alert threshold. Some represent expected delay; others reveal different definitions or a capture defect. The pilot's most important test is whether we can explain the divergence and assign responsibility for correction without assuming either side is always the truth.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Monitor divergence without creating another black box

blocks.text: I would separate three signal families: contract incompatibility, missingness incompatibility, and numeric differences under the same contract. Each leads to a different investigation. A different hash calls for deployment review; one-sided absence calls for checking availability and eligibility; different values call for examining events and transformations. Combining everything into one skew rate loses this information and makes it harder to prioritize a correction that could actually affect customer decisions.

Comparator coverage also needs to be visible. If we can reconstruct only simple features, the observed rate does not describe the whole system. I would show how many eligible decisions were compared, which versions were excluded, and why. Dimensions should be bounded to avoid unnecessary cost and exposure. A customer identifier must not become a time-series label. Individual investigation cases need a separate access and retention path with a defined purpose.

A useful alert would include the contract, window, magnitude, period, and owners of feature production and consumption. It would also indicate whether there is evidence of potentially affected decisions without automatically converting that evidence into financial loss. Where appropriate, I would evaluate whether divergence changes model output through a governed replay. This connects data quality to impact, but causal caution remains necessary: a changed score does not prove that a real decision was wrong.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Compatibility as part of the data rollout

blocks.text: A window or source change can be as important as a model release. I would treat feature evolution as a shared contract with a new version, boundary examples, and identified consumers. The producer should not replace the meaning while keeping the same name merely because the format is unchanged. Migration must allow the two definitions to be evaluated in parallel or establish a coordinated switch, depending on cost and existing platform constraints.

The pilot would begin with comparison that does not block decisions. This makes it possible to measure cost, coverage, and the rate of expected divergences. We could then introduce gates for unequivocal incompatibilities, such as a consumer requesting an unsupported contract. I would be more cautious about blocking on value differences because legitimate delays and incomplete capture may cause false alarms. Automation should follow the quality of divergence classification, not merely the technical availability of a blocking control.

As an EM, I would align data and service owners and reserve capacity to resolve cross-team problems. As a Staff engineer, I would define compatibility and how to preserve historical references. The return plan would cover not only code but also available data and versions. If migration removes the ability to reconstruct the previous definition, rollback may exist in name only. The contract must state how long old combinations remain operable and what evidence supports retiring them.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: Useful replays without indiscriminate copies

blocks.text: A comparator can become a powerful data consumer. I would avoid centralizing the entire history simply because it makes debugging easier. I would start with references, governed samples, and aggregates, choosing the minimum needed to reproduce the feature. Access must respect the investigation's purpose, with appropriate retention and query auditing. Explaining a decision does not require everyone with dashboard access to explore every financial event that preceded it.

Computational cost also needs limits. Recalculating long windows for every decision can multiply queries and harm source systems. I would assess sampling, snapshots, and aggregate reuse without losing temporal semantics. An optimization that conveniently uses future data is a correctness regression even if it reduces job duration. Evaluation must consider both performance and reconstruction fidelity, because both form part of the replay contract.

In the laboratory, the sum traverses in-memory events and is suitable only for fixture-sized inputs. There is no index, distributed storage, or query budget. A real implementation would need an access design consistent with volume and the existing platform. I would prefer demonstrating usefulness on a few critical features before expanding coverage. If the comparator creates high cost and unactionable divergences, the first adjustment should be to the question it is trying to answer, not the purchase of more capacity.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: ADR: compare by contract and instant

blocks.text: The proposed decision compares equivalent feature versions at the same instant and with the same knowledge cutoff. Comparing daily averages is inexpensive and may detect broad changes, but it does not explain decision-level divergence. Requiring exact equality for every feature ignores numeric characteristics and legitimate delays. I would combine an explicit contract, sampled point-in-time comparison, and aggregate metrics, calibrating each part to the chosen feature's nature.

The cost lies in maintaining contract identity, temporal references, and replay capability. This may require producer and consumer changes as well as governance over historical data. Not every feature warrants that investment. I would prioritize those with high potential impact, complex transformations, or a history of hard-to-explain divergence. The decision should consider the expected benefit of detecting an error and the cost of investigating false alarms, avoiding treating every variation as an operational incident.

I would revisit the ADR when the definition cannot be faithfully reconstructed or comparison yields little useful signal. In those cases, producer contract tests, distribution monitoring, or governed capture at decision time may be better alternatives. The goal is not to prove batch and online are always identical. It is to make explicit when they should be, which differences are acceptable, and what action to take when reality exceeds those agreed limits.

pages.chapter_title: The same feature in training and at decision time

pages.title: A shared contract needs owners

blocks.text: The first increment could cover one feature with a versioned definition, executable examples, online capture, and limited replay. Acceptance would include explaining at least one missingness case, one late event, and one contract change without rewriting the past. As an EM, I would bring together those producing, transforming, and consuming the data, reserving time to correct the divergences found. A platform alone cannot resolve semantic disagreement; someone must decide which meaning serves the domain and own its maintenance.

The value model would begin with recoverable investigation time and incompatibility incidents actually avoided. Reducing inappropriate decisions would require further evaluation without attributing every loss change to the comparator. I would separate storage, processing, and human-review costs. Hours saved represent potential capacity, not automatic savings. I would also record traceability benefits that have no simple monetary conversion, such as explaining a behavioral change and reducing uncertainty before a significant release.

My Staff question would be: does this feature describe what happened, what was known, or what was corrected later? My EM question would be: when two teams disagree on the answer, is there a fast, respectful process to decide and update the contract? Quality emerges from the combination. A hash and test suite make the definition verifiable; collaboration and responsibility keep it correct as the product and organization change.
