pages.chapter_title: Wesley Vieira · a proposal for Nubank

pages.title: From my experience to the team’s stack.

rows: Paired reviews of code and incidents.

blocks.text: Joining a new organization means learning how it makes decisions. I would start with one complete flow: from the gesture in the app to the service, event, persistence, and support. From there, I would identify what is standard, where exceptions exist, and which commitments were made to sustain current operations.

The functional lab included in this edition demonstrates that approach. It runs in Clojure and separates state transformation from external effects. This does not replace experience with the internal platform; it narrows the distance between saying I learn a language and showing an artifact that can be reviewed. The same standard applies to management: explain how I would learn from the team before promising reorganization.

blocks.title: The first delivery I would aim for
blocks.text: A small, observable, reversible improvement built with people who know the domain. The initial objective is to earn context and trust through the work.

pages.chapter_title: Wesley Vieira · a proposal for Nubank

pages.title: Clojure: decisions as data.

blocks.text: The functional core receives one state and returns another. An invalid transition produces an explicit error; it does not call a network, queue, or database. This separation allows the contract to be discussed before infrastructure is chosen. Within the model, versioning prevents an old intent from changing a newer state.

blocks.code:
(def transitions
  {:received #{:pending :rejected}
   :pending #{:settled :rejected}
   :settled #{}
   :rejected #{}})

(defn advance [db key expected-version next-status]
  (let [{:keys [status version] :as current} (get db key)]
    (when-not current
      (throw (ex-info "unknown operation" {:reason :not-found})))
    (when-not (= expected-version version)
      (throw (ex-info "stale writer" {:reason :version-conflict})))
    (when-not (contains? (get transitions status #{}) next-status)
      (throw (ex-info "illegal transition"
                      {:reason :illegal-transition})))
    (assoc db key (assoc current :status next-status
                         :version (inc version)))))
blocks.caption: Excerpt from decision_core.clj; local execution verified. In-memory model without networking.

blocks.text: The excerpt is part of decision_core.clj, executed in Clojure 1.12.0 on Java 17. The complete file has 11 tests and 22 assertions. Value immutability provides neither durable persistence nor distributed exclusion: when integrating a database, version comparison and writing must share the same atomic boundary.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Clojure: repetition does not create another intent.

blocks.text: The idempotency key identifies intent; the fingerprint identifies its relevant content. Repeating the same key with the same value preserves state. Reusing it with a different value is a conflict, not a new purchase. In the synthetic example, key scope is the in-memory database; production would need customer, operation, and retention policy.

blocks.code:
(defn register [db {:keys [key amount currency] :as cmd}]
  (when-not (valid-command? cmd)
    (throw (ex-info "invalid command"
                    {:reason :invalid-command})))
  (let [fingerprint [amount currency]
        existing (get db key)]
    (cond
      (nil? existing)
      (assoc db key {:fingerprint fingerprint
                     :status :received :version 0})
      (= fingerprint (:fingerprint existing)) db
      :else
      (throw (ex-info "key reused with different payload"
                      {:reason :key-conflict})))))

;; Em um único processo: atualização atômica do modelo.
;; Nunca adicionar efeitos externos à função de swap!.
(def state (atom {}))
(swap! state register
       {:key "synthetic-001" :amount 1250 :currency :BRL})
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the local lab; valid-command? is defined in the complete file. Concurrency test executed.

blocks.text: The concurrency test submits eighty identical registrations against an atom and verifies one entry. This exercises local atomicity; it does not demonstrate exactly-once processing between services. Production still needs authenticated identity, persistence, expiration control, reconciliation, and a consistent response when the connection drops after commit.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Datomic: identity and decision history.

blocks.text: The model separates operation identity from state evolution. The identity constraint prevents the same operation being represented as two entities. Version compare-and-swap accompanies the status change in the transaction. This is an educational proposal, not a description of Nubank's schema.

blocks.code:
;; Schema proposto para um exercício de domínio.
[{:db/ident :operation/id
  :db/valueType :db.type/uuid
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one
  :db/unique :db.unique/identity}
 {:db/ident :operation/status
  :db/valueType :db.type/keyword
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one}
 {:db/ident :operation/version
  :db/valueType :db.type/long
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one}]

;; Uma transação propõe a mudança de versão e status.
;; entity-id e expected-version são obtidos pelo adapter.
[[:db/cas entity-id :operation/version
  expected-version (inc expected-version)]
 [:db/add entity-id :operation/status :operation/pending]]
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: A correct version alone does not guarantee a valid business transition. The adapter must validate the state machine and ensure the observed condition belongs to the authorized transaction. History helps explain decisions but requires retention policy and care not to persist unnecessary sensitive data. Exact semantics depend on the edition and API the team adopts.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Kafka: contract before topic.

blocks.text: The proposed envelope carries event identity, aggregate identity, and domain version. Each answers a different question: have I processed this delivery, which operation does it belong to, and where does it fit in the sequence? The consumer must not confuse a transport offset with a business version.

blocks.code:
{
  "event_id": "synthetic-event-001",
  "event_type": "operation.status_changed",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "aggregate_id": "synthetic-operation-001",
  "aggregate_version": 2,
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
  "producer": "proposed-operation-service",
  "correlation_id": "synthetic-correlation-001",
  "payload": {
    "previous_status": "pending",
    "status": "settled",
    "currency": "BRL",
    "amount_minor": 1250
  }
}
blocks.caption: Proposed JSON contract with synthetic identifiers; not an internal Nubank event.

blocks.text: The partition key must reflect the unit for which order matters. Reprocessing a message requires idempotency in the effect, not just the producer. A Kafka transaction does not automatically turn an external call or a write to another database into a single global transaction. The relevant test interrupts the consumer between persistence and acknowledgment and observes recovery.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: AWS / DynamoDB: arbitrate the first write.

blocks.text: A conditional reservation makes key creation a competition resolved by storage. A service must not perform query-then-insert as two independent operations and assume exclusivity. Scope prevents a customer's key from being confused with another intent.

blocks.code:
# Exemplo de adapter com boto3; cliente e tabela são externos.
# Nomes e valores são sintéticos.
def reserve(table, scope, request_key, fingerprint):
    pk = f"IDEMPOTENCY#{scope}#{request_key}"
    return table.put_item(
        Item={
            "pk": pk,
            "fingerprint": fingerprint,
            "status": "reserved",
            "version": 0,
        },
        ConditionExpression="attribute_not_exists(pk)",
    )

# Uma ConditionalCheckFailedException exige consultar
# o registro: replay compatível ou conflito de payload.
# Não converter todo erro em 'já processado'.
# A expiração da chave precisa respeitar a janela de replay.
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: Reservation is not settlement. If the process crashes after reserving and before submitting the operation, pending work must be distinguished from completed work. Reserved state needs recovery with ownership and a time bound. Expiration policy must not allow a late retry to repeat a financial effect already performed.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Kubernetes: availability during change.

blocks.text: The example reserves capacity for one additional replica while gradually removing the previous version. Readiness should indicate whether an instance can receive work; it must not fluctuate with every shared-dependency failure and remove the entire service simultaneously. The numbers are educational assumptions.

blocks.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: proposed-journey-reader
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: journey-reader}
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate: {maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: journey-reader}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: reader
          image: example.invalid/reader:replace-with-reviewed-digest
          ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /ready, port: 8080}
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: "250m", memory: "256Mi"}
            limits: {memory: "512Mi"}
blocks.caption: Reference manifest, deliberately without an executable image. Not applied to a cluster.

blocks.text: Before applying it, a reviewed image, service identity, network policies, graceful shutdown, concurrency limits, and distribution across zones would be required. Three replicas in the same failure domain do not fail independently. Rollout must observe journey completion and saturation as well as count ready pods.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Flutter: state drives the interface.

blocks.text: The component receives domain state; it does not infer completion from an absent spinner. A pending message must remain true when the network fluctuates. The design avoids offering retry while the financial outcome remains unknown; the next action depends on the reconciliation contract.

blocks.caption: Reference Flutter/Dart excerpt; not compiled in this edition.

blocks.text: The example needs widget, screen-reader, text-scaling, and real-navigation tests. A live region can announce a change without moving focus, but excessive announcements also harm the experience. Final wording should be developed with Design and Content, including expected time, a safe action, and a help channel when the delay is no longer normal.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Dart: states that do not contradict one another.

blocks.text: A collection of booleans can represent impossible combinations: loading and completed, no receipt and available. A closed set of states makes these possibilities more visible. Here, a confirmed receipt requires its own identifier; query unavailability is not presented as an operation failure.

blocks.caption: Educational Dart 3 example; not compiled in this edition.

blocks.text: Typing helps implementation, but the server remains authoritative for financial state. The client must handle old contract versions and unknown responses. Fallback should preserve confirmed data without inventing a new success state. The proposal must be validated against the team's Dart version and modeling conventions.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Prometheus: measure a promise.

blocks.text: Numerator and denominator must observe the same population. If abandoned journeys disappear from instrumentation, latency can look better while the experience gets worse. The measurement contract must define start, completion, timeout, legitimate cancellation, and missing events.

blocks.caption: Proposed PromQL queries; not executed on a Prometheus server.

blocks.text: Aggregated percentiles require care with buckets and distributions. A percentile alone reveals neither volume nor success rate; it must be read alongside counts, errors, and segmentation. Labels need bounded cardinality. Account, operation, and customer identifiers belong in controlled diagnostic trails, not time-series labels.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: OpenTelemetry: follow causality.

blocks.text: A trace should explain relationships between operations, not merely enumerate calls. Payment confirmation can cross synchronous and asynchronous stages, retries, and reconciliation. Sampling must retain enough failure and high-latency examples for investigation.

blocks.code:
# Fragmento de instrumentação; tracer fornecido pelo runtime.
def confirm(command, repository, tracer):
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("journey.confirm") as span:
        span.set_attribute("journey.kind", "payment")
        span.set_attribute("contract.version", 1)
        try:
            result = repository.confirm(command)
            span.set_attribute("journey.outcome", result.kind)
            return result
        except TimeoutError:
            span.set_attribute("journey.outcome", "unknown")
            raise

# Não registrar CPF, token, saldo ou payload integral.
# Propagar contexto entre produtores e consumidores.
# Para processamento assíncrono, modelar links/parentesco
# de acordo com a semântica real do trabalho.
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: A trace does not replace a durable financial record. It may be sampled, delayed, or missing precisely during an incident. Diagnostics should associate an operation with a trace through controlled access while keeping personal data out of common attributes. The goal is shorter investigations without creating another indiscriminate repository of sensitive information.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Java / JVM: explicit budgets.

blocks.text: A timeout for each dependency can add up to more time than the journey allows. A shared budget forces every stage to account for time already consumed. A monotonic clock suits duration within a process; distributed timestamps require another contract and tolerance for clock differences.

blocks.caption: Reference Java excerpt; not compiled as a program in this edition.

blocks.text: Canceling a wait does not undo a remote effect. After a timeout, the outcome may remain unknown and require reconciliation. This is where my JVM experience connects to the financial domain: controlling threads and connections is necessary, but retry decisions depend on idempotency, authority, and state. The example is not a complete HTTP client.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Python: an experiment must be allowed to fail.

blocks.text: Python can quickly make a behavioral hypothesis concrete. A useful test describes an observable consequence, such as blocking expansion when the sample is insufficient. The code example is a deterministic gate, not a statistical significance test. The threshold must come from an approved journey policy.

blocks.caption: Educational example separate from the twenty executed labs; synthetic threshold.

blocks.text: The twenty case labs use synthetic data and local tests. They help detect contract regressions, illegal states, and representation errors. They do not measure Nubank's infrastructure, estimate real load, or certify production controls. Each chapter records exactly what the lab covers and what requires additional validation.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: PostgreSQL: integrity in storage.

blocks.text: The schema makes certain invariants impossible to ignore accidentally: positive amount, supported currency, and a unique key per scope. The update conditions the transition on state and version. If no row returns, the service must distinguish conflict, replay, and a nonexistent identifier.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE proposed_operation (
  operation_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_scope TEXT NOT NULL,
  request_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_minor BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_minor > 0),
  currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL CHECK (currency = 'BRL'),
  version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (version >= 0),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
    status IN ('received','pending','settled','rejected')
  ),
  UNIQUE (customer_scope, request_key)
);

UPDATE proposed_operation
SET status = 'pending', version = version + 1
WHERE operation_id = $1
  AND version = $2
  AND status = 'received'
RETURNING operation_id, version, status;
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: PostgreSQL is an educational option in this book, not an inference about every Nubank domain's database. A status constraint limits vocabulary but does not express the complete state machine. Transaction, indexes, isolation, and outbox strategy must be evaluated together so persistence and publication recover coherently from failures.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Redis: cache with domain validity.

blocks.text: Cache policy starts with a product question: how much delay can this data tolerate? An informational projection may accept brief validity; financial authorization may require the authoritative source. The same tool can be appropriate for one path and unsuitable for another.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: TTL bounds duration but does not prevent a late write from reinstalling an older version. Distributed implementation needs version comparison, invalidation, or another workload-appropriate strategy. The example deliberately omits that mechanism and identifies it as remaining work. Redis is a proposed alternative, not a claim about Nubank's internal design.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Terraform: reviewable changes.

blocks.text: Infrastructure as code makes decisions available for review: ownership, recovery, resource identity, and protection against accidental removal. Someone capable of assessing impact must interpret the plan; it should not be approved merely because the file passed formatting.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: prevent_destroy replaces neither access control nor backup policy. Removing the configuration block or changing the management strategy requires additional care. The example was not applied and includes no remote backend, provider version, managed key, or IAM policy. These omissions are explicit so an editorial excerpt does not look production-ready.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: TypeScript: validate the boundary.

blocks.text: A static type does not validate JSON received at runtime. The proposed parser treats the boundary as unknown and rejects states outside the contract. In a product, rejection must become a safe experience with an alternative query or incompatibility message, without inventing financial confirmation.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: TypeScript is used here for contracts and visualization, not as a general Nubank requirement. For a real SDK, I would generate types from a versioned schema, maintain fixtures for old consumers, and define handling of additional fields. Safe evolution expands the contract without forcing every client to update simultaneously.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: Grafana: a dashboard that guides action.

blocks.text: The dashboard starts with the decision someone needs to make. Confirmed completion, unknown state, and reconciliation age describe different aspects of trust. CPU and memory aid diagnosis but do not independently demonstrate that the customer completed the task.

blocks.caption: Conceptual dashboard specification; not Grafana's import schema.

blocks.text: The JSON is an editorial specification, not an importable Grafana dashboard. Each indicator needs a definition, denominator, window, owner, and connection to the response procedure. Red without an agreed action creates noise. A good dashboard also displays missing data and small samples so telemetry silence is not interpreted as success.

pages.chapter_title: Foundations and technologies

pages.title: One journey, two authorities.

blocks.title: One journey, two authorities.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: The architecture separates the authority that changes state from the authority that presents it. The domain core and its storage decide whether an operation was accepted. The projection makes reading easier, but carries version and lag. A screen cannot turn a missing update into rejection, and support cannot promise reversal without consulting the state responsible for the effect.

The outbox represents publication intent within the same boundary as the domain write. A publisher may repeat messages, so the consumer must deduplicate effects. The design allows failures between stages and makes recovery part of the contract. The choice between Datomic, DynamoDB, or another persistence option depends on the domain and existing platform; all three are not added simultaneously for aesthetic reasons.

The Clojure lab demonstrates only the in-memory decision. The case labs explore specific properties. Distributed integration, authorization, retention, and capacity still require validation in the team's context.

pages.chapter_title: Architectures connecting the cases

pages.title: Recovery as part of the product.

blocks.title: Recovery as part of the product.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: Recovery should not be a collection of ownerless exceptions. The flow must distinguish technical inability, suspected fraud, and insufficient evidence. Each may require a different path. Human review belongs where it adds judgment, not as an unlimited destination for every integration error.

The record associates decision, policy, and validity. An old signal must not authorize a sensitive action indefinitely. When an alternative is denied, the product must explain the next available step without disclosing details that help bypass controls. This language requires collaboration between Security, Product, Content, and Support.

Success combines legitimate resolution, recovery time, and protection. Reducing a queue by rejecting more people can improve an operational metric while worsening the outcome. As EM, I would ensure capacity and responsibilities; as Staff, I would define authority, expiration, and review mechanisms.

pages.chapter_title: Architectures connecting the cases

pages.title: An experience platform with contracts.

blocks.title: An experience platform with contracts.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: A server-driven interface platform increases composition speed, but also increases the importance of its contract. The installed client may lag behind the server version. The validator must understand the renderer's minimum capability and prevent a configuration requiring nonexistent behavior.

Fallback is a product component: it must preserve the task and accessibility, not merely prevent crashes. Telemetry connects configuration, app version, and journey outcome. The gate requires sufficient evidence before expanding exposure. The decision retains an owner; it is not delegated to one context-free metric.

Nubank publishes work on BDC; this design is an educational proposal for discussing governance and evolution. I would investigate existing controls and seek the smallest necessary extension. The platform creates value when it reduces consumer-team effort while maintaining quality and recovery capability.

pages.chapter_title: Architectures connecting the cases

pages.title: ML: separate prediction from decision.

blocks.title: ML: separate prediction from decision.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: A score is not a business decision. Policy combines prediction with limits, context, and review paths. Separating these responsibilities allows a threshold to change without pretending the model was retrained and supports investigation into whether the problem lies in data, inference, or use of the result.

Features need identity and time: what was available when a decision was made may differ from what we know today. Evaluating with future information creates an impression of quality that would not exist in production. The training-serving contract must prevent this leakage and measure relevant differences.

Ground truth may arrive late and remain incomplete. Experiments must preserve version trails and treat false positives as legitimate people harmed by a decision. The proposed value is to improve protection and recovery together, with specialists responsible for policy and exposure criteria.

pages.chapter_title: Architectures connecting the cases

pages.title: The problem begins when the state becomes invisible

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.

blocks.text: The public post dated July 15, 2026 describes access to the app followed by errors in transfers, Pix payments, and the support channel. This raises an engineering question, not a diagnosis: how can guidance remain available when the primary operation fails? The report does not establish that the entire customer base was affected, that an incorrect debit occurred, or that the components share infrastructure. The analysis respects that boundary and proposes an investigation that can be verified.

I would distinguish three problems that can look identical on screen: unavailability before a command is accepted, an unknown outcome after acceptance, and unavailable status information. The first permits another attempt when safe; the second requires a query or reconciliation; the third requires a message that preserves the uncertainty. A single “try again” button can conceal these differences and lead customers to create unnecessary new operations.

The product objective would be to help people understand whether their money moved, what they can do next, and how to get help. The corresponding technical objective would be consistency between operation identity, the financial decision, and communication. This chapter’s lab tests the local part of that promise: a committed debit has a durable receipt and does not become another debit when the response is lost.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: An operation is an entity; an attempt is an event

blocks.text: The proposed domain distinguishes operation_id from request_id. An operation represents a stable intention: an account, a beneficiary, and an amount. An attempt represents a transport interaction, with its own timestamp, deadline, and network outcome. Confusing the two identifiers makes every retry look like a new intention. Under the suggested contract, the app retains operation_id while establishing the outcome of that same intention; changing the amount or beneficiary requires a new confirmation and another identifier.

Useful states would include received, rejected, confirmed, and outcome awaiting clarification. “Timeout” describes the attempt and must not, by itself, mark the operation as rejected. A confirmed state must reference a durable decision. An unavailable query must not erase a previously known confirmation either. For the interface, this means retaining the receipt and context through connectivity changes while distinguishing local information from confirmation obtained from the service.

The invariants are concrete: a nonnegative balance, one operation identity bound to a single payload, and agreement between the debit, ledger entry, and receipt. Session recovery adds another condition: an old session cannot issue new commands after the revocation barrier. These rules can be tested without knowing the bank’s internal architecture and allow candidate implementations to be evaluated before discussing language or infrastructure.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Separate the financial path from the guidance path

blocks.title: Separate the financial path from the guidance path
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: The design proposes two observable paths: executing a financial intention and clarifying an existing one. Authority over the debit remains with the decision service and its transactional record. A query projection can help scale reads, but it must disclose lag and cannot invent a confirmation. If it is stale, the query must consult the authoritative source or communicate that a reliable answer is not yet available.

Help appears as a separate domain because its minimum useful content should survive degradation of the financial path. This does not automatically require another cluster: shared dependencies, authentication, configuration, and capacity limits would need to be identified first. A static guidance page may address part of the problem while account information remains protected.

Kafka is an option for propagating confirmed events; it does not make an external write part of a distributed atomic transaction. The proposed implementation would need recoverable publication, an idempotent consumer, and reconciliation. The lab demonstrates only the local transaction and makes that boundary explicit.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: The existing receipt takes precedence over the retry

blocks.code:
def pay(self, *, account_id, operation_id, amount_cents,
        payee, recovery_epoch, fault=None):
    # Recorte: validação e payload/digest estão no arquivo completo.
    with self._write() as connection:
        account = connection.execute(
            "SELECT balance_cents, recovery_epoch FROM accounts "
            "WHERE account_id=?", (account_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if account is None:
            raise UnknownAccount(account_id)
        # A sessão é validada antes inclusive de retornar um recibo já existente.
        if recovery_epoch != account["recovery_epoch"]:
            raise StaleSession("Comando de sessão anterior à recuperação")
        previous = connection.execute(
            "SELECT payload_json, payload_hash, receipt_json "
            "FROM payments WHERE operation_id=?",
            (operation_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if previous is not None:
            # Compara também o conteúdo canônico, sem depender apenas do hash.
            if (previous["payload_hash"] != digest
                    or previous["payload_json"] != payload):
                raise IdempotencyConflict(
                    "operation_id reutilizado com outro payload")
            return json.loads(previous["receipt_json"])
        if account["balance_cents"] < amount_cents:
            raise InsufficientFunds("Saldo insuficiente no cenário sintético")
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the pay method; setup and writes omitted. The complete file was executed and verified.

blocks.text: The excerpt checks the session generation before revealing any outcome. It then looks up the operation identity and compares the canonical content as well as its hash. A valid retry returns the stored receipt; reusing the identity with another payload creates a conflict. Only a previously unseen intention reaches the balance check.

This order matters: the balance after the first purchase may be lower than the original amount, but that should not turn a replay into “insufficient funds.” In the SQLite model, the block executes inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Serialization is a local teaching choice, not a recommendation for distributed scale.

pages.title: Clojure: separate pure decisions from transactional effects

blocks.code:
(defn payment-decision [account previous command]
  ;; Contrato proposto; não é código interno do Nubank.
  (let [{:keys [epoch balance-cents]} account
        {:keys [session-epoch payload]} command
        amount (:amount-cents payload)]
    (cond
      (not= epoch session-epoch)
      {:type :reject :reason :stale-session}

      (and previous (not= payload (:payload previous)))
      {:type :reject :reason :idempotency-conflict}

      previous
      {:type :replay :receipt (:receipt previous)}

      (or (not (integer? amount)) (not (pos? amount)))
      {:type :reject :reason :invalid-amount}

      (< balance-cents amount)
      {:type :reject :reason :insufficient-funds}

      :else
      {:type :commit
       :new-balance (- balance-cents amount)
       :payload payload})))
blocks.caption: Proposed teaching function; this Clojure excerpt was not executed.

blocks.text: The proposed function returns a decision as data. It does not write, call services, or guarantee concurrency safety on its own. Its purpose is to make the rules readable and allow combinations of state to be explored without a network dependency. The persistence layer must execute the decision against a valid view and confirm its preconditions atomically.

In a Datomic implementation, I would examine unique identity, version comparison, and the appropriate transaction before mapping this result to transaction data. Reading a balance and writing later without protection would retain the race, even with a correct pure function. The example is illustrative and was not executed in Clojure.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: The persistence contract: what must survive the process

blocks.text: The idempotency record cannot live only in the memory of the process that received the first attempt. Restarts, scaling, and instance replacement would make retries lose their history. In the local model, the payments table contains a unique operation_id, canonical content, and a receipt. The ledger table requires a unique operation identity and references the payment. The balance update occurs in the same transaction as both inserts, forming a single recovery unit.

The contract must specify how long that identity remains recognized. A short window may allow a disconnected client to resubmit an old intention as new; indefinite retention increases costs and data handling obligations. I would choose the window using retry data and operational needs, retaining enough identification to investigate disputes. This book does not establish an actual retention period for Nubank.

The receipt records the historical confirmation, including the balance observed after that decision. It must not be used as the current balance. A real integration would also require an external participant identity and settlement states that the lab does not implement. Guaranteeing a local entry does not guarantee that a remote system received the message exactly once. That distinction belongs in the contract, the runbook, and the explanation provided to the customer.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Concurrency must challenge the same invariant

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The first test releases two threads simultaneously and uses independent connections to compete for a balance that can fund only one purchase. The acceptable result is exactly one confirmation and one rejection for insufficient funds. In the second test, eight attempts represent the same intention and must converge on a single receipt.

The barrier increases the likelihood of overlap; it does not enumerate every possible interleaving. The 1,000-cent balance and 700-cent payments are synthetic fixtures. Subsequent checks verify the balance, record counts, and total debits. The test therefore observes financial effects, not just return codes.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Killing a process is different from raising an exception

blocks.code:
def run_crash_worker(self, fault: str, expected_exit: int):
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()),
         "--crash-worker", str(self.database), fault],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20,
    )
    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, expected_exit, result.stderr)
    self.bank = SyntheticPayments(self.database)

def test_process_crash_before_commit_rolls_back_and_resume_executes_once(self):
    self.run_crash_worker("crash_before_commit", 72)
    self.assert_invariants(balance=1000, payments=0)
    receipt = self.bank.pay(**self.command())
    self.assertEqual(self.bank.pay(**self.command()), receipt)
    self.assert_invariants(balance=300, payments=1)

def test_process_crash_after_commit_preserves_receipt_and_resume_replays(self):
    self.run_crash_worker("crash_after_commit", 73)
    self.assert_invariants(balance=300, payments=1)
    stored = json.loads(self.bank.inspect("alice")["payments"][0]["receipt_json"])
    self.assertEqual(self.bank.pay(**self.command()), stored)
    self.assert_invariants(balance=300, payments=1)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The tests start another process and terminate it with os._exit at defined points. Before the commit, reopening must find the balance unchanged; after the commit, it must find the persisted receipt. This distinction exercises recovery without relying on the finally block of an ordinary exception.

The complete file passed 12 tests, including these scenarios and a timeout after confirmation. The result does not prove resilience to power loss, disk corruption, or failure of an external provider. The evidence is narrower and more useful: in this local model, terminating the process at these two points does not create a duplicate debit on resumption.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Observe uncertainty, not just HTTP success

blocks.text: I would propose three families of signals. The first measures attempts: duration, transport errors, and saturation. The second measures operations: confirmations, identity conflicts, and time to resolve an unknown outcome. The third measures experience: successful queries, accessible help, and contacts associated with the incident. A fast HTTP response does not compensate for an operation that remains unresolved, and a transport error does not necessarily mean the financial decision was lost.

Proposed metrics could include payment_attempts_total with a bounded set of outcomes, payment_resolution_seconds by journey, and payment_unknown_operations as an aggregate count. Account identifiers, operation_id, and beneficiaries would not become Prometheus labels. Where needed and authorized, they belong in controlled investigations with appropriate correlation and retention. This decision avoids explosive cardinality and reduces unnecessary data exposure.

The incident dashboard would start with observable impact: how many intentions await clarification, is that number growing continuously, and is the help channel responding? Alerts should have an owner and an actionable response, such as reducing new admissions, initiating reconciliation, or publishing guidance. I would track percentiles and app version cohorts, but would not combine reconciliation queue time with command latency. They are different problems and need separate limits.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Release with a rollback path that preserves receipts

blocks.text: Rollout would begin with instrumentation and comparative reads, without changing the financial decision. A set of synthetic intentions would exercise timeouts and queries while the team checked whether identifiers travel through every layer. The first visible change could be a clearer state explanation and help route, provided the information was accurate. This can reduce confusion before replacing critical write mechanisms.

For the transactional component, I would require compatibility between versions during migration. The old version must recognize an operation written by the new one or be prevented from executing it again. An interface feature flag does not solve that compatibility problem. A safe strategy would maintain a shared record and stable read contracts, with clear criteria for halting expansion if unexpected conflicts, unresolved operations, or balance discrepancies increased.

In Kubernetes, traffic distribution and rollback would be operational controls, not guarantees of domain correctness. Reverting a binary must not erase idempotency records or restore an incompatible schema. I would prepare an exercise in which the new process commits, fails before responding, and the previous process handles the retry. Rollout would advance only after receipt continuity had been demonstrated and support could explain that path.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Limit repeated work without hiding the outcome

blocks.text: A retry storm can turn partial unavailability into saturation. I would use explicit deadlines, attempt budgets, and jittered backoff for repeated queries, separating these controls from financial identity. The client may wait longer before querying, but must not generate another operation merely because its network budget expired. A conflict response must also be distinguishable from a transient error, since repeating the same invalid payload does not help.

The query endpoint requires authorization appropriate to the sensitivity of the receipt. Knowing an operation_id cannot be sufficient to read another account’s data. The lab’s session generation demonstrates the ordering of the barrier, but the program receives parameters directly and does not implement real authentication. In a service, identity and generation would come from verified credentials, and queries would be scoped to the account holder.

For performance, I would measure contention before choosing a partitioning scheme. The lab serializes writers in the SQLite file, simplifying the local proof while limiting throughput. A distributed design would need to choose its consistency boundary and prevent unsafe concurrency on the same account. The Staff-level objective would be to remove unnecessary work from the critical path without moving financial authority into a potentially stale projection.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: ADR: durable receipts and recoverable publication

blocks.text: The proposed decision is to make local confirmation a durable fact and use that identity to answer retries. Keeping only a response cache would be simpler initially, but would leave a gap when the cache expired or an instance restarted. Blocking every retry would prevent some duplicates, yet would also prevent recovery of lost responses and transfer uncertainty to support.

To distribute the outcome, I would compare recoverable publication associated with the transaction, reading a change log, and synchronous integration with the consumer. The choice would depend on storage guarantees and available operational capabilities. In every option, the consumer must recognize the event identity and make its effect safe to repeat. A proposed Kafka topic must not be presented as proof of a single effect in external services.

The accepted consequence is greater attention to states, retention, and reconciliation. The intended benefit is a deterministic explanation for the customer and the incident investigator. I would revisit this decision if the settlement boundary required separate reservation and confirmation, if multiple currencies were involved, or if throughput pressure changed the unit of serialization. The ADR would record these conditions and the tests that must continue passing after any migration.

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: How I would lead delivery and demonstrate value

blocks.text: I would organize the initiative around a journey rather than a component list. A payments owner would define financial truth; mobile would validate how an intention survives connectivity changes; support would define the information needed to resolve a case; and platform would support isolation and operations. My role as an EM would be to turn those dependencies into verifiable deliverables and prevent responsibility for uncertainty from falling between teams.

The first review would require failure examples and permitted states. The second would demonstrate concurrency and recovery tests. The third would evaluate a simulation with support and communications, including how to explain an outcome that is still unknown. As a Staff engineer, I would review the transactional boundary, retry contracts, and migration decisions, documenting what the lab proves and what remains outside its scope. None of this requires attributing an unobserved architecture to the bank.

Value would be estimated as avoided contacts multiplied by marginal resolution cost, minus maintenance and infrastructure costs. Time to clarification and perceived trust would remain outcomes in their own right, without automatically converting them into revenue. The interview question I would bring is concrete: “Which component can assert that an intention was confirmed when the original response was lost, and how do we demonstrate that every client version can recover that truth?”

pages.chapter_title: When Pix fails, help fails too

pages.title: Security also needs a legitimate recovery path

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.

blocks.text: The NuCommunity participant reports that their front camera was broken, their rear camera worked, and they could not activate the account through facial recognition. The public excerpt does not reveal the outcome or any alternatives subsequently offered. It therefore does not establish a biometric failure. It provides a concrete case for examining how a security requirement behaves when a device lacks the expected capability.

A well-designed recovery process must protect two people: the legitimate account holder who has lost access and the account holder someone is trying to impersonate. Simplifying the path by ignoring identity evidence might resolve the first contact while creating a larger risk. My proposal would make exception handling predictable through capability checks, assisted routing, and trackable status while preserving the risk assessment required to restore access.

The engineering problem extends beyond the camera. It includes repeated attempts, deadlines, human review, device changes, and commands issued by old sessions. This chapter models those boundaries with a persistent state machine and a recovery generation. The lab does not perform liveness detection, face matching, or fraud assessment: it demonstrates how to prevent skipped steps, reuse of an expired decision, and repeated restoration of the same case. This boundary makes the work reviewable and avoids presenting a simulation as an identity system.

sources.title: NuCommunity — Unable to access my account; facial recognition required

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Device capability is not account-holder identity

blocks.text: I would separate technical diagnosis from identity assessment. The first determines whether a camera exists, permission has been granted, and capture can begin. The second decides whether the available evidence is sufficient for a sensitive action. An unavailable camera may route the case to another journey; it cannot, on its own, authorize access. This distinction prevents a device error code from inadvertently becoming a security exception.

The proposed states would be diagnosis, review, verified, restored, expired, and closed. Each transition has preconditions, an owner, and a version. History would preserve why a step occurred without requiring biometric images to circulate through every service. “Verified” means an authorized assessment has completed its step; “restored” means the access change has taken effect. Separating them makes it possible to detect an approval still awaiting application.

The local model uses two distinct reviewers to make separation of responsibility explicit. This is a synthetic policy, not a universal recommendation for manual operations. In production, the mix of automation and review would depend on risk and governance. The transferable principle is that applying a decision must check its scope, validity, and version at the moment access is restored, including when messages arrive late.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Recovery with a boundary between evidence and authorization

blocks.title: Recovery with a boundary between evidence and authorization
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: The proposal keeps sensitive evidence within a restricted boundary and uses references to track the case. Support needs to know the stage and next action, but not every operator needs access to biometric material. Restoration goes through the identity authority, which records the session generation and confirms application. The tracking screen receives only the data needed to guide the account holder.

The delicate point is the gap between approval and execution. If a decision expires or is revoked while awaiting processing, the consumer must reject it. A duplicate message must recover the existing result. The case version acts as a precondition, while the session generation prevents old commands from remaining valid after recovery.

A real implementation would require reviewer authentication, role-based authorization, protected storage, and access auditing. The lab demonstrates transitions with fictional names and SQLite; it does not provide those identity or operational guarantees.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: A transition validates version, deadline, and actor

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The read and update take place inside a write transaction. The expected revision prevents two operators from applying decisions against the same version. The deadline is checked before every transition, including restoration. The actor must be different from the requester and, for final application, also different from the previous reviewer.

In the lab, these actors are strings supplied by the test, so they do not constitute authentication. The value lies in the domain rule, which remains visible and verifiable. In a real implementation, the actor and permissions would be derived from a trusted credential, and each decision would leave an appropriate audit record. The function does not validate biometrics.

pages.title: Datomic: version as an explicit precondition

blocks.code:
(defn restore-tx [case-id expected-version now decision]
  ;; Esboço proposto de dados transacionais.
  ;; O chamador autenticado precisa validar a autorização.
  (when-not (= :verified (:state decision))
    (throw (ex-info "case-not-verified" {})))
  (when (>= now (:expires-at decision))
    (throw (ex-info "decision-expired" {})))
  (let [new-version (inc expected-version)
        identity-id (:identity-id decision)
        old-epoch (:recovery-epoch decision)]
    [[:db/cas case-id
      :recovery/version expected-version new-version]
     [:db/cas case-id
      :recovery/state :verified :restored]
     [:db/cas identity-id
      :identity/recovery-epoch old-epoch (inc old-epoch)]
     {:db/id "audit-event"
      :audit/kind :recovery-restored
      :audit/case case-id
      :audit/decision-id (:decision-id decision)
      :audit/actor-id (:actor-id decision)
      :audit/at now}]))
blocks.caption: Datomic/Clojure sketch with proposed attributes; not executed.

blocks.text: The sketch uses transactional comparisons to prevent a decision from being applied after the version, state, or generation has changed. The data format and attributes are proposed. The aim is to discuss atomicity between the case change, identity change, and audit record without claiming that Nubank uses this schema.

Checking a deadline before submitting the transaction is insufficient if the wait is long. The final implementation would need to guarantee validity at the point of application, according to the capabilities and transaction model selected. The excerpt was not executed in Datomic; this gap is a review requirement, not an implicit guarantee.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Evidence has a different lifecycle from the case

blocks.text: A case identifier may be needed for support longer than an image collected for a specific verification. I would model references and retention policies separately, avoiding copies of sensitive material in logs, general-purpose events, or tracking tools. A completed-stage event should carry the decision, its provenance, and the authorized scope, not an indiscriminately attached bundle of personal documents.

The proposed contract would include case_id, revision, status, expires_at, and reason_category with a controlled vocabulary. Customer-facing details would differ from investigation details. An understandable category such as “we need to confirm some information” can provide guidance without exposing thresholds or signals used to detect abuse. The contract must not promise a deadline operations cannot yet meet; it must distinguish an estimate, a commitment, and the absence of a forecast.

Reopening a case also requires an explicit decision. Reusing an old approval may be unsafe after a device change or a change in risk. Creating a new revision preserves the link to history without treating previous evidence as permanent authorization. In the lab, expiration rejects new transitions; there is no automatic deletion or regulatory policy. Those capabilities would be defined with identity, privacy, and support owners before any use with real people.

pages.title: Test the rule a shortcut would try to bypass

blocks.code:
# Validação dos limites de autoridade e validade.
def test_restore_requires_two_distinct_reviewers(self):
    verified = self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "reviewer-a", 101)
    self.assertEqual(verified["state"], "verified")
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "reviewer-a", 102)
    result = self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "reviewer-b", 102)
    self.assertEqual((result["state"], result["epoch"]), ("restored", 1))

def test_owner_cannot_verify(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "customer", 101)
    self.assertEqual(self.store.read("case")["revision"], 0)

def test_expired_case_cannot_restore(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "expired"):
        self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 400)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The tests challenge three shortcuts: the same reviewer approving and restoring access, the requester verifying their own identity, and a decision being applied after its deadline. Each rejection must preserve the previous state. The test does not ask whether a screen displayed a message; it verifies that the prohibited mutation did not happen.

These restrictions are governance fixtures for the simulation. A real team could adopt another approval policy, provided the rule was explicit and tested. The important question in a Staff-level review is who has authority over each transition and how that authority remains valid under repetition and delay.

pages.title: Resuming a case must not repeat restoration

def test_stale_revision_cannot_repeat_verification(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "stale_revision"):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "b", 102)

def test_reopen_preserves_case_and_epoch(self):
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    reopened = Recovery(self.path)
    self.assertEqual(reopened.read("case")["revision"], 1)
    reopened.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 102)
    self.assertEqual(Recovery(self.path).read("case")["epoch"], 1)

def test_cannot_skip_review_or_restore_twice(self):
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 0, "restore", "b", 101)
    self.store.transition("case", 0, "verify", "a", 101)
    self.store.transition("case", 1, "restore", "b", 102)
    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
        self.store.transition("case", 2, "restore", "c", 103)
    self.assertEqual(self.store.read("case")["epoch"], 1)
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: Reopening the Recovery object uses the same persisted file, demonstrating that the version and generation do not depend on the previous instance’s memory. The other tests reject a stale revision, an attempt to skip verification, and a second restoration.

All seven tests in the file passed, including checks for an invalid clock and revision type. They cover the local machine and its preconditions, but do not exercise concurrency with authenticated operators, real queues, or identity services. Nor do they measure biometric quality. The next implementation experiment would inject duplicate delivery and revocation between approval and application while retaining the same criterion: no access change without a valid decision.

pages.title: Measure the queue without exposing its members

blocks.text: The central metric would be time to completed legitimate recovery, broken down by stage and technical reason for routing. An average alone would hide people stuck for days while simple cases finish quickly. I would track the tail of waiting times, the age of the oldest case, and repeat-contact rate, as well as the proportion of requests returning to the same stage without useful new information.

A second dimension measures protection: restorations later disputed, rejected attempts to use expired decisions, and blocked commands from old generations. These numbers must not reward a team for denying everything, nor should speed encourage approval without sufficient evidence. The dashboard must show both sides of the decision and support qualitative sample reviews with controlled access to details.

I would avoid identifying people, specific devices, or reviewers in aggregate metric labels. Individual investigations would remain in audit trails with a defined purpose and permissions. For accessibility, useful segmentation would follow the observed barrier, such as an unavailable camera or reading difficulty, without turning collection into intrusive classification. The intended result is to locate the operational and technical bottleneck with enough information to act while retaining the minimum necessary information about each account holder.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Launch exception paths with support prepared

blocks.text: The first delivery would not be a new identity algorithm. It would detect the technical failure earlier and prevent a futile sequence of capture attempts. A message could explain that the component is unavailable and route the person to the existing assisted path. This behavior should be validated with people using broken cameras, denied permissions, and limited-capability devices, including use with assistive technology.

Next, I would introduce case tracking to a controlled cohort. Support would need access to the same state the customer sees, differing only in the permitted level of detail. A migration that creates more states without preparing operators can increase transfers between teams. Each new state would therefore have an operational action, an owner, and an understandable exit criterion.

Automated restoration or identity integration would follow only after authorization, expiration, and revocation had been validated in a test environment. Rollback would keep open cases queryable and prevent reapplication of already confirmed decisions. I would define an operational intake limit so that the new journey did not collect requests faster than the team could review them. The experience must be sustainable for both the customer and the person resolving the exception.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Accessibility is part of the security surface

blocks.text: Ambiguous instructions can make people repeat movements, seek unsuitable environments, or share information through the wrong channels. I would treat journey clarity as a security control: explain what will be requested, where information is sent, and what happens next. That does not mean revealing fraud rules. It means reducing the gap between a legitimate action and an improvised workaround that exposes the customer.

In the proposed Flutter interface, states would need accessible semantics, stable focus order, and announcements that do not rely exclusively on color or animation. A camera failure must not disappear so quickly that a screen reader cannot announce it. Validation would include enlarged text and app interruption, because recovery often takes place under less comfortable conditions than an ideal onboarding flow.

For performance, I would reduce repeated collection and loading steps that do not change the decision. The client could query status at a moderate frequency while relevant updates were propagated recoverably. The priority is not approval at any cost, but removing waits that add no verification. If a stage takes time because it depends on a person, the app should acknowledge that and provide accurate tracking rather than an endless spinner that looks like a technical failure.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: ADR: an explicit recovery process with limited authorization

blocks.text: The proposed decision is to represent recovery as a domain process separate from everyday login. One alternative would embed every exception in the same capture flow. That would simplify initial navigation, but make it difficult to understand attempts that span support, device replacement, and review. Another alternative would resolve everything manually through messages, providing considerable flexibility but little consistency in state, authorization, or tracking.

I would choose an explicit process because it makes the validity of each decision clear and limits what each step authorizes. Verifying a document need not mean enabling every financial operation. Restored access may require further risk checks under the applicable policy without turning the state machine into a universal shortcut. Those policies would be product and security decisions, not deductions from the public report.

The accepted cost is maintaining contracts between identity, review, and support. The design must also avoid bureaucracy: states should exist only when they change responsibility, authorization, or useful information. I would revisit the ADR if most exceptions could be resolved through reliable local diagnosis, if manual operations became the dominant bottleneck, or if new device capabilities reduced the need for collection. The choice would be reviewed against evidence of legitimate resolution and protection, not the number of steps.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: EM execution: the capacity to resolve cases, not merely receive them

blocks.text: As an EM, I would begin with a workshop on real cases already authorized for analysis, bringing together support, identity, risk, mobile, and accessibility. The output would be a matrix of barriers, owners, and existing paths. The broken-camera report would inform one category without being used to claim prevalence. I would separate improvements to clarity, process changes, and authorization changes because they have different risks and dependencies.

The plan would have small deliverables: understandable diagnosis, routing with context, shared state, and transactional integration with identity. Each would require a demonstration under failure, an operational review, and the capacity to track outcomes. As a Staff engineer, I would focus on decision validity across boundaries, session generation, and persistent transitions. The lab is an artifact for technical discussion, not a substitute for security review.

Value could be calculated through support minutes avoided, fewer repeat contacts, and shorter periods without access for legitimate account holders. Any retention gain would require an appropriate comparison, and fraud costs or additional review costs would be deducted. The leadership question would be: “Are we removing a barrier that adds no security, or simply shifting work to another team?” The answer must be visible in case resolution and protection metrics, not just screen conversion.

pages.chapter_title: Recovering access when the front camera does not work

pages.title: Enough information, deliberate disclosure

blocks.caption: Original source screenshot, accessed 23 October 2026. An individual report is not a reproduced incident.
Screenshot published by a customer on NuCommunity, kept in Portuguese. Context and limitations are available in the source.

blocks.text: The public suggestion collects examples of investment income, cashback, and bill notifications that, according to the author, omitted amounts. The attached images provide context for the complaint, but do not reveal all privacy preferences or the version currently available. The opportunity is not to conclude that every notification should display money. It is to build a content policy that helps people decide while respecting the disclosure context they have chosen.

I would begin by asking what task the message enables someone to complete. An alert may confirm that something happened, request an action, or highlight a deadline. Each purpose needs different fields. An amount may prevent an unnecessary app opening; on a locked screen visible to other people, the same amount may disclose information the account holder would prefer to keep private. The experience must make this choice understandable rather than accidental.

This chapter’s proposal combines an event contract, a message catalog, versioned preferences, and late enforcement of the privacy policy. The lab queues synthetic facts, changes the preference before sending, and verifies the final content. It does not connect to push providers. Its purpose is to show that the moment at which a policy is evaluated is part of system correctness, just as much as the sentence displayed on screen.

sources.title: NuCommunity — Nubank app push notifications omit the amount (suggestions)

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: A financial fact is not notification copy

blocks.text: A domain event should describe what happened without embedding a ready-made sentence for a particular language or device. The communication catalog interprets that fact, decides whether there is a relevant message, and applies the presentation policy. Separating these responsibilities allows copy to be corrected without changing event semantics and privacy to evolve without requiring every financial producer to understand each mobile platform’s particularities.

The proposed contract contains event_id, schema version, event type, account holder, and only the necessary data. Preferences have a different lifecycle: they can change while a message waits in the queue. Storing final copy with an exposed amount when the event is produced would therefore be insufficient. The proposal reads the current policy close to delivery and includes its version in the operational evidence.

There are at least four communication states: eligible, suppressed, accepted by the provider, and displayed or opened when that information is available. Acceptance does not prove reading, and the absence of an open event does not prove failure. The lab models only local acceptance and suppression. Product decisions must avoid treating “sent” as certainty that the customer learned about a financial fact or had an effective opportunity to act.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Render close to delivery and record the decision

blocks.title: Render close to delivery and record the decision
blocks.caption: Original proposed design; it does not represent Nubank’s internal architecture.

blocks.text: The renderer is the boundary where a financial fact becomes text potentially visible outside the app. It needs the current preference and catalog version. If the preference query is unavailable, the proposed policy falls back to content without an amount or suppresses the message, depending on its purpose. Consent is not assumed because the preferences service is down.

The queue preserves event identity and version; duplicates must not generate repeated messages indefinitely. The audit record captures the communication decision and its policy parameters, avoiding storage of the sensitive body when a controlled reference is enough. The external provider remains an important boundary: after it accepts a payload, withdrawing it may no longer be possible.

Kafka would be an asynchronous transport option, but would not replace deduplication of the effect at the provider boundary. The lab keeps its queue and deduplication in memory to isolate content rules, without claiming durability or actual delivery.

pages.title: Apply privacy at the last controllable point

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: The method first recognizes a delivery already accepted in the model and avoids repeating it. For a pending message, it reads the current preference. The default hides the amount; disclosure requires explicit enablement. Monetary formatting uses divmod on integer cents, without binary floating-point rounding.

The “accepted” result is only the simulated provider’s response. After that point, changing the preference cannot recall a message already delivered, and the lab makes no such promise. A real implementation would also need to bound the interval between reading the preference and sending, handle an unavailable read, and document the revocation boundary.

pages.title: Clojure: a message catalog as data

blocks.code:
(def templates
  {:income {:title "Atualização financeira"
            :private-body "Consulte os detalhes no aplicativo."}
   :cashback {:title "Cashback disponível"
              :private-body "Veja a atualização no aplicativo."}})

(defn cents-label [cents]
  (str "R$ " (quot cents 100) ","
       (format "%02d" (mod cents 100))))

(defn render-message [event preference]
  ;; Catálogo e contrato propostos; sem envio neste exemplo.
  (when-not (= 1 (:schema-version event))
    (throw (ex-info "unsupported-schema" {})))
  (when-not (true? (:enabled? preference))
    (throw (ex-info "communication-suppressed" {})))
  (let [template (get templates (:kind event))
        amount (:amount-cents event)]
    (when-not (and template (integer? amount) (<= 0 amount))
      (throw (ex-info "invalid-event" {})))
    {:title (:title template)
     :body (if (true? (:show-values? preference))
             (str "Crédito disponível: " (cents-label amount))
             (:private-body template))
     :policy-version (:version preference)}))
blocks.caption: Proposed catalog and function; Clojure not executed.

blocks.text: The example makes the catalog inspectable and keeps the privacy decision in a function separate from transport. This facilitates tests of wording, amounts, and preference combinations. The field names and sentences are proposals in this book, not actual Nubank contracts.

A production catalog would need governance for translation, accessibility, and purpose, alongside disclosure review. The function does not resolve the race between revocation and sending, nor does it replace authorization to query account-holder information. It must not receive unvalidated monetary values from arbitrary sources either. This Clojure excerpt is educational and was neither compiled nor executed.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Version content without breaking older consumers

blocks.text: The event schema and message version solve different problems. The former defines fields and meaning; the latter identifies how those fields were presented. A title change may be compatible with the same event, whereas introducing a new financial state may require a consumer update. I would record these versions separately so that investigations do not have to reconstruct communication from the code running in production today.

In transport, event_id must remain stable when a producer repeats publication. Deduplication must detect the same identifier reappearing with different content, since that signals a contract error. The lab rejects this reuse. For a real persistent queue, I would define retention, partitioning, and handling of unrecognized events, ensuring that a producer update could not silently suppress critical messages without alerting the owner.

Preferences also need versions to explain which policy was applied. That does not authorize storing a complete history of personal information inside the event. A minimal operational record can reference a policy and a decision, with restricted access to details when necessary. In the customer’s settings, the configuration must have a stable meaning: “hide amounts in notifications” must not accidentally hide only some categories. Any exceptions should be explicit and justified.

pages.chapter_title: A notification should help someone decide

pages.title: Reject ambiguity before generating copy

blocks.caption: Excerpt from the synthetic lab; execution verified in the complete file.

blocks.text: Input validation checks the set of fields, integer version, category, and monetary type. Reusing event_id with different content creates a conflict. Preferences require actual booleans: the string false cannot be interpreted as permission to expose amounts. A valid configuration increments the preference version, making it possible to recognize that a communication decision occurred under a different policy.

The model is deliberately strict: a producer adding fields must negotiate the contract instead of relying on silent acceptance. That choice suits the lab; a real platform could adopt extensible compatibility with well-defined rules. The in-memory queue does not survive a restart, so the tests on this page verify semantics, not transport reliability.
